name: Ab Wheel Rollout
setupNotes: Kneel with the hands on the wheel under the shoulders. Set the gear up within reach so the set starts without scrambling.
targetNotes: Roll forward keeping the ribs down and hips slightly tucked. Pull back with the abs before the back arches.
trainerTip: Roll only as far as you can keep a neutral spine — the range will come.

name: Air Bike
setupNotes: Set the saddle so your knee keeps a slight bend at the bottom of the stroke. Set the saddle height so your knee keeps a slight bend at the bottom of the stroke.
targetNotes: Ride the planned interval or steady block. Track time and distance where the console allows.
trainerTip: The air bike punishes power output — great for intervals, brutal for the ego.

name: Arnold Press
setupNotes: Seated or standing, hold the dumbbells at chest height with palms facing you. Set the dumbbells within reach and plant your stance before you pick them up.
targetNotes: Press up while rotating the palms to face forward at the top. Reverse the rotation on the way down.
trainerTip: The rotation sweeps through the whole delt — go light enough to keep it smooth.

name: Band Calf Raise
setupNotes: Stand on a band with the balls of your feet and pull the ends up to your shoulders. Pre-stretch the band to your start position so every rep begins under tension.
targetNotes: Lower the heels to a full stretch, then press up onto the toes against the band.
trainerTip: Slow negatives replace heavy load here — the band keeps constant tension.

name: Band Chest Fly
setupNotes: Set your shoulders back and keep a soft, fixed bend in the elbows. Pre-stretch the band to your start position so every rep begins under tension.
targetNotes: Open your arms in a wide arc until you feel a stretch across the chest. Squeeze the arms back together over mid-chest, not over your face.
trainerTip: Think of hugging a barrel — the arc does the work, not a press.

name: Band Curl
setupNotes: Stand tall with the weight at arm's length and the elbows pinned to your ribs. Pre-stretch the band to your start position so every rep begins under tension.
targetNotes: Curl to shoulder height without letting the elbows travel forward. Lower all the way to straight arms.
trainerTip: The elbows are hinges bolted to your sides — every inch they drift forward steals biceps.

name: Band External Rotation
setupNotes: Set the pulley at waist height and stand side-on, elbow bent 90° and glued to your ribs. Pre-stretch the band to your start position so every rep begins under tension.
targetNotes: Rotate the arm away from the pulley keeping the elbow pinned. Return slowly.
trainerTip: It feels like nothing and does everything for shoulder longevity.

name: Band Face Pull
setupNotes: Set the rope at upper-chest height and step back into tension. Pre-stretch the band to your start position so every rep begins under tension.
targetNotes: Pull the rope toward your face, splitting the hands beside your ears. Return with control.
trainerTip: Finish with external rotation — posture insurance for desk-bound shoulders.

name: Band Front Raise
setupNotes: Stand on the band with feet hip-width and hold the ends at your thighs. Pre-stretch the band to your start position so every rep begins under tension.
targetNotes: Raise straight arms to shoulder height against the band. Lower with control.
trainerTip: The band's tension grows toward the top — where the front delts need it least, so keep it light.

name: Band Glute Kickback
setupNotes: Set the ankle cuff on the low pulley and face the stack with hands braced. Pre-stretch the band to your start position so every rep begins under tension.
targetNotes: Drive the cuffed leg straight back to full hip extension. Return with control without arching the back.
trainerTip: Range and squeeze beat stack weight — this is a finisher, not an ego lift.

name: Band Hip Abduction
setupNotes: Set the machine pads against your outer thighs and sit square. Pre-stretch the band to your start position so every rep begins under tension.
targetNotes: Press your legs outward to your full pain-free range. Return slowly without letting the weight slam.
trainerTip: Glute medius is the knee's bodyguard — do not skip it just because the loads look small.

name: Band Hip Thrust
setupNotes: Set your upper back on a bench with the barbell padded over your hips and feet planted. Pre-stretch the band to your start position so every rep begins under tension.
targetNotes: Drive the hips to full lockout with the chin tucked and ribs down. Lower to a hover and repeat.
trainerTip: Chin tucked and eyes forward — a lifted chin borrows from the glutes and hands the change to the lower back.

name: Band Lat Pulldown
setupNotes: Anchor the band overhead (door frame or pull-up bar) and kneel or sit below it. Pre-stretch the band to your start position so every rep begins under tension.
targetNotes: Pull the ends down to your shoulders driving the elbows into the pockets. Return to a full overhead stretch.
trainerTip: A home pull-down stand-in — slow negatives make up for the light load.

name: Band Lateral Raise
setupNotes: Stand tall with the weights at your sides and a slight forward lean. Pre-stretch the band to your start position so every rep begins under tension.
targetNotes: Raise the arms out to shoulder height leading with the elbows. Lower slowly — no free fall.
trainerTip: Light weight and honest reps; think of a tiny forward tilt at the top like pouring water.

name: Band Lateral Walk
setupNotes: Loop a band above your knees and drop into a half-squat. Pre-stretch the band to your start position so every rep begins under tension.
targetNotes: Step sideways keeping constant band tension. Travel one way, then come back.
trainerTip: Stay in the half-squat for the whole set — standing up between steps lets the burn escape.

name: Band Leg Extension
setupNotes: Set the pad just above your ankles and adjust the seat back. Sit tall and loop the band around your ankle, anchoring it behind you.
targetNotes: Extend to a full lockout and squeeze the quad for a beat. Lower under control, never dropping the stack.
trainerTip: Pause at the top — riding the machine's momentum is why legs do not grow.

name: Band Overhead Extension
setupNotes: Hold the weight overhead with both hands, elbows narrow and pointing forward. Pre-stretch the band to your start position so every rep begins under tension.
targetNotes: Lower the weight behind your head by bending the elbows only. Extend to full lockout overhead.
trainerTip: The overhead position stretches the long head — the two-thirds of the triceps most lifts miss.

name: Band Overhead Press
setupNotes: Rack the bar on your front delts with elbows slightly ahead of it and feet hip-width. Pre-stretch the band to your start position so every rep begins under tension.
targetNotes: Press the bar overhead, moving your head back as it passes, finishing with biceps by the ears. Lock out tall with the ribs down.
trainerTip: Squeeze the glutes and brace — a leaking midsection steals more press than weak shoulders do.

name: Band Pallof Press
setupNotes: Stand side-on to a cable at chest height holding the handle at the sternum. Pre-stretch the band to your start position so every rep begins under tension.
targetNotes: Press the handle straight out, resisting the twist. Hold, return, and keep the ribs square.
trainerTip: The anti-rotation squeeze is the rep — if you are rotating, you are just pressing air.

name: Band Pull-Apart
setupNotes: Hold a band in front of you at shoulder width with arms straight. Pre-stretch the band to your start position so every rep begins under tension.
targetNotes: Pull the band apart to your chest, squeezing the shoulder blades. Return with control.
trainerTip: A hundred a day keeps the desk slump away — cheap posture medicine.

name: Band Pull-Through
setupNotes: Stand away from a low pulley with the rope between your legs. Pre-stretch the band to your start position so every rep begins under tension.
targetNotes: Hinge forward letting the arms travel back, then drive the hips forward to stand. Squeeze the glutes hard at the top.
trainerTip: It is a hip hinge in disguise — if your arms fatigue, you are pulling with them.

name: Band Push-Up
setupNotes: Set hands just outside shoulder width and step your feet back into one straight line. Loop the band over your upper back and pin both ends under your palms.
targetNotes: Lower until your chest is a fist off the floor with elbows tracking about 45°. Press the floor away and lock out without the hips sagging.
trainerTip: Squeeze your glutes and brace — a push-up is a moving plank.

name: Band Pushdown
setupNotes: Face a high pulley with the straight bar attached and elbows pinned to your sides. Pre-stretch the band to your start position so every rep begins under tension.
targetNotes: Extend to straight arms keeping the upper arms still. Let the weight return to a controlled 90°.
trainerTip: Pin the elbows — if they drift forward, the chest and lats start freelancing.

name: Band Rear Delt Fly
setupNotes: Hinge to 45° or rest chest-down on an incline bench with the weights hanging. Pre-stretch the band to your start position so every rep begins under tension.
targetNotes: Raise the arms out to the sides with a soft elbow bend, squeezing the shoulder blades. Lower slowly.
trainerTip: Lead with the pinkies and think 'thumbs up' — it is a fly, not a row.

name: Band Row
setupNotes: Anchor the band at mid height, sit or stand back to tension, and hinge slightly. Pre-stretch the band to your start position so every rep begins under tension.
targetNotes: Row the handles to your ribs squeezing the shoulder blades. Return to long arms under tension.
trainerTip: Step forward to ease the stretch between sets if the tension runs out of range.

name: Band Squat
setupNotes: Set the bar across your traps, unrack, and take a stance just outside shoulder width. Stand on the band's middle and pull the ends up to your shoulders.
targetNotes: Sit down between your hips until the hip crease passes the knee, or as deep as your back stays neutral. Drive up through mid-foot to stand tall.
trainerTip: Own the depth where you can keep a neutral spine — deeper at lighter load beats higher at max.

name: Band Straight-Arm Pulldown
setupNotes: Stand facing a high pulley with a bar or rope, arms straight, hinged slightly forward. Pre-stretch the band to your start position so every rep begins under tension.
targetNotes: Sweep the handle down to your thighs without bending the elbows. Let it rise to shoulder height for a full lat stretch.
trainerTip: If you cannot keep straight arms, the stack is too heavy — ego down, lats up.

name: Band Woodchopper
setupNotes: Set the pulley high or low and stand side-on with both hands on the handle. Pre-stretch the band to your start position so every rep begins under tension.
targetNotes: Pull diagonally across the body to the opposite hip, rotating through the ribs. Return with control.
trainerTip: High-to-low and low-to-high both deserve a turn — hit both directions in the week.

name: Band-Assisted Dip
setupNotes: Loop a band across the dip bars and kneel or step into its stretch. Pre-stretch the band to your start position so every rep begins under tension.
targetNotes: Lower to about 90° at the elbows with the band sharing the load. Press to straight arms.
trainerTip: Thinner band as you strengthen — the goal is band-free dips.

name: Band-Assisted Pull-Up
setupNotes: Loop a band over the bar and stand or kneel into it with your working foot or knee. Pre-stretch the band to your start position so every rep begins under tension.
targetNotes: Pull to chin over bar letting the band share the load. Lower slowly to a straight-arm hang.
trainerTip: Move to a thinner band every couple of weeks — the goal is kicking the band out entirely.

name: Banded Good Morning
setupNotes: Step onto a band looped around your upper back and hold the ends at your chest. Pre-stretch the band to your start position so every rep begins under tension.
targetNotes: Hinge at the hips against the band tension until the torso approaches parallel. Drive the hips forward to stand.
trainerTip: A gentle hinge variation — great as a warm-up or for rehab blocks.

name: Barbell Bench Press
setupNotes: Lie back with your eyes just under the bar and drive your shoulder blades down and together. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Lower the weight to mid-chest with elbows about 45° from your torso. Press up and slightly back to lockout without losing the packed shoulders.
trainerTip: Grip wide enough that your forearms stay vertical at the bottom, and only use depth you can control every single rep.

name: Barbell Bulgarian Split Squat
setupNotes: Place your rear foot on a bench behind you and hop the front foot to a squat-length stance. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Drop the back knee toward the floor until the front thigh is parallel. Drive up through the front mid-foot.
trainerTip: Lean the torso slightly forward for glutes, stay upright for quads — a great exercise either way.

name: Barbell Curl
setupNotes: Stand tall with the weight at arm's length and the elbows pinned to your ribs. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Curl to shoulder height without letting the elbows travel forward. Lower all the way to straight arms.
trainerTip: The elbows are hinges bolted to your sides — every inch they drift forward steals biceps.

name: Barbell Floor Press
setupNotes: Sit on the floor, press the weight to arm's length above your chest, then lie back and plant your feet. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Lower your elbows until they lightly touch the floor. Press up from that dead stop.
trainerTip: The dead stop kills the bounce — honest lockout strength for pressing sticking points.

name: Barbell Front Raise
setupNotes: Stand tall holding the weights in front of your thighs. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Raise straight arms to shoulder height. Lower with control back to the thighs.
trainerTip: Front delts already work in every press — keep this volume small and deliberate.

name: Barbell Glute Bridge
setupNotes: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat and close to your hips. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Drive through the heels lifting the hips to a straight line. Squeeze the glutes at the top, then lower slowly.
trainerTip: Squeeze at the top like you are pinching a coin — two seconds minimum.

name: Barbell High Pull
setupNotes: Hold the bar at hip height with an overhand grip and knees soft. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Explode the hips and shrug while pulling the bar to chest height with high elbows. Catch it at the hips.
trainerTip: Fast hips and loose arms — the pull rides the explosion, it does not make it.

name: Barbell Jump Squat
setupNotes: Set your squat stance with no load or a very light bar. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Drop to a quarter squat and jump as high as possible. Absorb the landing into your next rep.
trainerTip: Maximum intent on every rep — power training at half speed trains nothing.

name: Barbell Preacher Curl
setupNotes: Set your armpits over the top of the pad with the arms stretched along it. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Curl to just under chin height. Lower to near-full extension without locking hard.
trainerTip: The pad forbids cheating — half-reps here are extra obvious, so do not.

name: Barbell Pullover
setupNotes: Lie along or across a bench holding one weight in both hands above your chest. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Lower the weight in an arc overhead until it levels with your head. Pull it back over your chest keeping the arms nearly straight.
trainerTip: Keep the ribs down — if your back arches to buy range, you have gone too far.

name: Barbell Reverse Wrist Curl
setupNotes: Rest your forearms on a bench with the wrists over the edge, palms down. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Lower the weight down, then raise the backs of your hands as high as they go.
trainerTip: The extensors balance all that gripping — elbow health insurance.

name: Barbell Rollout
setupNotes: Kneel with the hands on the wheel under the shoulders. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Roll forward keeping the ribs down and hips slightly tucked. Pull back with the abs before the back arches.
trainerTip: Roll only as far as you can keep a neutral spine — the range will come.

name: Barbell Row
setupNotes: Hinge to roughly 45° or flatter and brace your trunk before you touch the weight. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Drive your elbows back past your torso until the weight reaches your lower ribs. Lower under control to a full stretch without rounding.
trainerTip: Row with a still torso — if your hips pump, the load is writing cheques your back cannot cash.

name: Barbell Shrug
setupNotes: Stand tall holding the weight with your shoulders pulled down and back. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Shrug your shoulders straight up toward your ears. Lower to a full stretch with control.
trainerTip: Straight up and straight down — rolling the shoulders adds injury risk, not growth.

name: Barbell Squat
setupNotes: Set the bar across your traps, unrack, and take a stance just outside shoulder width. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Sit down between your hips until the hip crease passes the knee, or as deep as your back stays neutral. Drive up through mid-foot to stand tall.
trainerTip: Own the depth where you can keep a neutral spine — deeper at lighter load beats higher at max.

name: Barbell Standing Calf Raise
setupNotes: Set the pads over your shoulders (or hold the weight) with the balls of your feet on the edge. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Drop the heels to a full stretch. Press up onto the toes as high as possible.
trainerTip: Pause one full second at the top and the bottom — bouncing is the calf-raise cheat code.

name: Barbell Step-Up
setupNotes: Set a box at knee height and place your whole foot on top. Set the box on a flat, non-slip surface before you start.
targetNotes: Drive through the top leg to stand fully tall over the box. Lower with the same leg — no push-off from the floor.
trainerTip: No bouncing off the bottom leg — that is a cheating hand on the scales.

name: Barbell Walking Lunge
setupNotes: Stand tall with the weight held at your sides or in the front rack. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Step forward and lower until the back knee hovers at the floor. Push through the front leg to step into the next rep.
trainerTip: Long steps bias the glutes and short steps the quads — choose on purpose.

name: Barbell Wrist Curl
setupNotes: Rest your forearms on a bench with the wrists hanging over the edge, palms up. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Let the weight roll down to your fingertips, then curl it back up through full wrist flexion.
trainerTip: The full roller-coaster range — fingertips to full squeeze.

name: Battle Ropes
setupNotes: Anchor the ropes' midpoint and grip an end in each hand in a quarter squat. Set the gear up within reach so the set starts without scrambling.
targetNotes: Create waves, slams, or whips for the planned interval. Track time.
trainerTip: Soft knees and a braced core — the ropes love a lazy trunk.

name: Bayesian Cable Curl
setupNotes: Face away from a low pulley with the handle behind you and the arm extended back. Set the pulley height first, then test the travel with a light pin before loading.
targetNotes: Curl forward and up from the stretched position. Lower back behind you under tension.
trainerTip: Peak contraction meets loaded stretch — light weight and maximal intent.

name: Bear Crawl
setupNotes: Set up on hands and toes with the knees hovering and hips level with the shoulders. Brace hard before the first rep — there is no external load to do it for you.
targetNotes: Crawl forward moving the opposite hand and foot together. Keep the hips low and level.
trainerTip: A moving plank with a cardio tax — short, controlled bursts first.

name: Bear Plank
setupNotes: Set up on hands and toes with the knees hovering an inch off the floor, under the hips. Brace hard before the first rep — there is no external load to do it for you.
targetNotes: Hold the table-top hover with a flat back and stacked shoulders for time.
trainerTip: The knees never touch down — one inch of hover, all abs.

name: Behind-the-Neck Press
setupNotes: Rack the bar on your traps as in a back squat with hands wide. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Press straight overhead from behind the neck to lockout. Lower behind the neck with control.
trainerTip: Only for shoulders that pass the mobility bar — position first, load second.

name: Belt Squat
setupNotes: Load the machine and belt, then step onto the platform with the weights hanging free. Adjust the seat and handle height so the pad meets the working joint.
targetNotes: Squat to full depth with an unloaded spine — no bar on your back. Stand driving through mid-foot.
trainerTip: All legs and zero axial load — a lifesaver on tired-back weeks.

name: Bench Dip
setupNotes: Place your hands on a bench behind you, heels forward, hips off the bench. Check the bench angle and anchor points before you set up.
targetNotes: Lower the hips toward the floor, bending the elbows straight back. Press up to straight arms.
trainerTip: Keep the hips close to the bench — drifting forward turns it into a shoulder stretch.

name: Bicycle Crunch
setupNotes: Lie back with the hands by the ears and the legs lifted. Brace hard before the first rep — there is no external load to do it for you.
targetNotes: Rotate the elbow toward the opposite knee while the other leg extends. Alternate smoothly.
trainerTip: Rotate from the ribs, not the elbows — slow and deliberate beats a pedal frenzy.

name: Bird Dog
setupNotes: Set up on all fours with the hands under the shoulders and a flat back. Brace hard before the first rep — there is no external load to do it for you.
targetNotes: Extend the opposite arm and leg until level with the torso. Hold a beat, return, and switch sides.
trainerTip: A long, quiet line beats a high, fast kick — imagine balancing a mug on your back.

name: Bodyweight Squat
setupNotes: Set the bar across your traps, unrack, and take a stance just outside shoulder width. Brace hard before the first rep — there is no external load to do it for you.
targetNotes: Sit down between your hips until the hip crease passes the knee, or as deep as your back stays neutral. Drive up through mid-foot to stand tall.
trainerTip: Own the depth where you can keep a neutral spine — deeper at lighter load beats higher at max.

name: Box Jump
setupNotes: Set a stable box at a height you can land on softly. Set the box on a flat, non-slip surface before you start.
targetNotes: Dip into a quarter squat and jump onto the box, landing quietly. Step back down — never bounce off.
trainerTip: Land like a ninja; if you are crashing, the box is too high.

name: Box Squat
setupNotes: Set a box to parallel height and take a wide stance with the bar low on your back. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Sit back onto the box keeping the shins vertical, pause a beat, then drive off it. Finish tall with the glutes locked.
trainerTip: The pause must be dead — a touch-and-go box squat is just a squat with furniture.

name: Bradford Press
setupNotes: Rack the bar on your front delts as an overhead press. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Press overhead and lower behind the neck, then press back overhead and down to the front. Keep moving.
trainerTip: Light and smooth — it is a circulation and mobility drill with a barbell.

name: Broad Jump
setupNotes: Stand with feet hip-width behind a clear runway. Brace hard before the first rep — there is no external load to do it for you.
targetNotes: Load a quarter squat and jump forward as far as possible. Stick the landing solidly.
trainerTip: Measure your jumps — competing with yourself is the best progression.

name: Bulgarian Split Squat
setupNotes: Place your rear foot on a bench behind you and hop the front foot to a squat-length stance. Set the dumbbells within reach and plant your stance before you pick them up.
targetNotes: Drop the back knee toward the floor until the front thigh is parallel. Drive up through the front mid-foot.
trainerTip: Lean the torso slightly forward for glutes, stay upright for quads — a great exercise either way.

name: Burpee
setupNotes: Clear a patch of floor with nothing valuable in sight. Brace hard before the first rep — there is no external load to do it for you.
targetNotes: Kick back to a plank, chest to floor, jump the feet in, and explode upward. Repeat.
trainerTip: Pace them — a burpee you cannot repeat is not a rep, it is a decision.

name: Butt Kicks
setupNotes: Stand tall with the arms relaxed at your sides. Brace hard before the first rep — there is no external load to do it for you.
targetNotes: Jog in place, flicking the heels up toward the glutes with quick, light contacts.
trainerTip: A hamstring and calf primer — stay tall and spring off the balls of the feet.

name: Cable Chest Press
setupNotes: Set both pulleys at shoulder height and step forward of the cables with one foot staggered. Set the pulley height first, then test the travel with a light pin before loading.
targetNotes: Press the handles forward until your arms lock out level with your chest. Let them return until your hands pass your shoulders slightly.
trainerTip: The cables fight you at lockout — where the bench press gets easy, this stays hard.

name: Cable Crossover
setupNotes: Set both pulleys high, step forward into a staggered stance, and hinge slightly at the hips. Set the pulley height first, then test the travel with a light pin before loading.
targetNotes: Sweep the handles down and together until your hands meet in front of your hips. Let them return with control to a chest stretch.
trainerTip: One step forward from the cables keeps constant tension — never let the stack rest between reps.

name: Cable Crunch
setupNotes: Lie on your back with the knees bent and hands by the ears. Kneel below a high pulley holding the rope beside your ears.
targetNotes: Curl the shoulder blades off the floor, exhaling hard. Lower slowly, one vertebra at a time.
trainerTip: Curl the ribs toward the hips — pulling on the neck is banned.

name: Cable Curl
setupNotes: Stand tall with the weight at arm's length and the elbows pinned to your ribs. Set the pulley height first, then test the travel with a light pin before loading.
targetNotes: Curl to shoulder height without letting the elbows travel forward. Lower all the way to straight arms.
trainerTip: The elbows are hinges bolted to your sides — every inch they drift forward steals biceps.

name: Cable External Rotation
setupNotes: Set the pulley at waist height and stand side-on, elbow bent 90° and glued to your ribs. Set the pulley height first, then test the travel with a light pin before loading.
targetNotes: Rotate the arm away from the pulley keeping the elbow pinned. Return slowly.
trainerTip: It feels like nothing and does everything for shoulder longevity.

name: Cable Fly
setupNotes: Set your shoulders back and keep a soft, fixed bend in the elbows. Set the pulley height first, then test the travel with a light pin before loading.
targetNotes: Open your arms in a wide arc until you feel a stretch across the chest. Squeeze the arms back together over mid-chest, not over your face.
trainerTip: Think of hugging a barrel — the arc does the work, not a press.

name: Cable Front Raise
setupNotes: Stand tall holding the weights in front of your thighs. Set the pulley height first, then test the travel with a light pin before loading.
targetNotes: Raise straight arms to shoulder height. Lower with control back to the thighs.
trainerTip: Front delts already work in every press — keep this volume small and deliberate.

name: Cable Glute Kickback
setupNotes: Set the ankle cuff on the low pulley and face the stack with hands braced. Set the pulley height first, then test the travel with a light pin before loading.
targetNotes: Drive the cuffed leg straight back to full hip extension. Return with control without arching the back.
trainerTip: Range and squeeze beat stack weight — this is a finisher, not an ego lift.

name: Cable Hammer Curl
setupNotes: Hold the weights with a neutral grip — palms facing in — at your sides. Set the pulley height first, then test the travel with a light pin before loading.
targetNotes: Curl straight up keeping the palms facing each other throughout. Lower fully.
trainerTip: Hits the brachialis that pushes the biceps up — pair it with regular curls.

name: Cable Kickback
setupNotes: Hinge over with the elbows bent and pinned at your sides. Set the pulley height first, then test the travel with a light pin before loading.
targetNotes: Extend both arms straight back, squeezing the triceps at the top. Return only to the elbow bend.
trainerTip: The upper arm stays frozen like a statue — everything else is decoration.

name: Cable Lateral Raise
setupNotes: Stand tall with the weights at your sides and a slight forward lean. Set the pulley height first, then test the travel with a light pin before loading.
targetNotes: Raise the arms out to shoulder height leading with the elbows. Lower slowly — no free fall.
trainerTip: Light weight and honest reps; think of a tiny forward tilt at the top like pouring water.

name: Cable Pull-Through
setupNotes: Stand away from a low pulley with the rope between your legs. Set the pulley height first, then test the travel with a light pin before loading.
targetNotes: Hinge forward letting the arms travel back, then drive the hips forward to stand. Squeeze the glutes hard at the top.
trainerTip: It is a hip hinge in disguise — if your arms fatigue, you are pulling with them.

name: Cable Pullover
setupNotes: Lie along or across a bench holding one weight in both hands above your chest. Set the pulley height first, then test the travel with a light pin before loading.
targetNotes: Lower the weight in an arc overhead until it levels with your head. Pull it back over your chest keeping the arms nearly straight.
trainerTip: Keep the ribs down — if your back arches to buy range, you have gone too far.

name: Cable Pushdown
setupNotes: Face a high pulley with the straight bar attached and elbows pinned to your sides. Set the pulley height first, then test the travel with a light pin before loading.
targetNotes: Extend to straight arms keeping the upper arms still. Let the weight return to a controlled 90°.
trainerTip: Pin the elbows — if they drift forward, the chest and lats start freelancing.

name: Cable Rear Delt Fly
setupNotes: Hinge to 45° or rest chest-down on an incline bench with the weights hanging. Set the pulley height first, then test the travel with a light pin before loading.
targetNotes: Raise the arms out to the sides with a soft elbow bend, squeezing the shoulder blades. Lower slowly.
trainerTip: Lead with the pinkies and think 'thumbs up' — it is a fly, not a row.

name: Cable Reverse Curl
setupNotes: Hold the weight with an overhand grip at arm's length. Set the pulley height first, then test the travel with a light pin before loading.
targetNotes: Curl to shoulder height keeping the wrists straight and firm. Lower with control.
trainerTip: The forearms will give out first — that is the design, not a fault.

name: Cable Rope Curl
setupNotes: Attach the rope to a low pulley and grip the ends with palms up. Set the pulley height first, then test the travel with a light pin before loading.
targetNotes: Curl the rope toward your shoulders keeping the elbows pinned. Return to full extension.
trainerTip: Split the rope apart at the top for a squeeze the straight bar cannot give.

name: Cable Shrug
setupNotes: Stand tall holding the weight with your shoulders pulled down and back. Set the pulley height first, then test the travel with a light pin before loading.
targetNotes: Shrug your shoulders straight up toward your ears. Lower to a full stretch with control.
trainerTip: Straight up and straight down — rolling the shoulders adds injury risk, not growth.

name: Cable Side Bend
setupNotes: Hold one dumbbell at your side with the other hand on your hip. Set the pulley height first, then test the travel with a light pin before loading.
targetNotes: Bend sideways toward the weight, lowering it along the thigh. Pull back to tall with the opposite obliques.
trainerTip: One weight only — two weights cancel the whole point.

name: Cable Upright Row
setupNotes: Hold the weight in front of your thighs with an overhand grip. Set the pulley height first, then test the travel with a light pin before loading.
targetNotes: Pull straight up to chest height keeping the elbows above the hands. Lower slowly.
trainerTip: Stop at chest height — pulling to the chin is where shoulders start complaining.

name: Cable Woodchopper
setupNotes: Set the pulley high or low and stand side-on with both hands on the handle. Set the pulley height first, then test the travel with a light pin before loading.
targetNotes: Pull diagonally across the body to the opposite hip, rotating through the ribs. Return with control.
trainerTip: High-to-low and low-to-high both deserve a turn — hit both directions in the week.

name: Chest Dip
setupNotes: Support your weight on parallel bars and lean your torso forward slightly. Test the bar height and lock your shoulders down before descending.
targetNotes: Lower until your upper arms reach parallel with a forward lean. Drive up to lockout squeezing through the chest, not just the triceps.
trainerTip: Leaning forward shifts work to the chest; staying upright makes it a triceps move.

name: Chin-Up
setupNotes: Hang with a supinated shoulder-width grip. Wipe the bar and set your grip width before you jump up.
targetNotes: Pull until your chin clears the bar keeping your chest tall. Lower to a dead hang every rep.
trainerTip: The underhand grip brings your biceps to the party — usually good for a few extra reps over pull-ups.

name: Clamshell
setupNotes: Lie on your side with knees bent and a band above your knees. Pre-stretch the band to your start position so every rep begins under tension.
targetNotes: Open your top knee like a clamshell keeping the heels together. Close slowly.
trainerTip: A tiny movement with a giant glute-medius payoff — a warm-up regular.

name: Clap Push-Up
setupNotes: Set a standard push-up position with a mat or soft floor under your hands. Brace hard before the first rep — there is no external load to do it for you.
targetNotes: Lower with control, then drive up hard enough to clap before landing. Absorb the landing with bent elbows.
trainerTip: Quality over quantity — end the set the moment claps turn into grazes.

name: Clean and Jerk
setupNotes: Set your clean grip and position the bar over mid-foot. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Clean the bar to your shoulders, then dip and drive it overhead, splitting the feet to catch. Recover to standing with the bar locked out.
trainerTip: Two lifts in one rep — grind the clean and you will have nothing left for the jerk.

name: Close-Grip Bench Press
setupNotes: Grip the bar just inside shoulder width and set your usual bench position. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Lower to your lower chest with the elbows tucked. Press up keeping the wrists stacked over the elbows.
trainerTip: Shoulder-width, not hands-touching — 'close' is relative to your bench.

name: Close-Grip Floor Press
setupNotes: Sit on the floor, press the weight to arm's length, and lie back with a narrow grip. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Lower the elbows to the floor with the arms tucked. Press up from the dead stop.
trainerTip: Triceps get the lockout work without the shoulder strain at the bottom.

name: Close-Grip Lat Pulldown
setupNotes: Use a neutral close-grip attachment and sit tall. Set the pulley height first, then test the travel with a light pin before loading.
targetNotes: Pull the handles to your sternum with elbows tracking past your ribs. Stretch fully at the top without shrugging.
trainerTip: The neutral grip is shoulder friendly — use it when the wide grip bothers your joints.

name: Close-Grip Pull-Up
setupNotes: Hang with palms facing each other on narrow parallel handles. Wipe the bar and set your grip width before you jump up.
targetNotes: Pull your chin over your hands with elbows tracking back. Descend to a straight-arm hang.
trainerTip: The friendliest pull-up for cranky shoulders — own it before adding load.

name: Concentration Curl
setupNotes: Sit on a bench and brace your elbow against your inner thigh. Set the dumbbells within reach and plant your stance before you pick them up.
targetNotes: Curl up with a slight wrist supination at the top. Lower slowly to full extension.
trainerTip: The brace isolates one biceps completely — no torso, no momentum, just arm.

name: Copenhagen Plank
setupNotes: Set a side plank with the top foot elevated on a bench and the bottom leg hanging. Check the bench angle and anchor points before you set up.
targetNotes: Hold the side plank supported by the top leg, hips high and body straight, for time.
trainerTip: A groin-strength powerhouse — start with short holds and the knee bent on the bench.

name: Cossack Squat
setupNotes: Stand wide with toes forward and arms extended in front. Brace hard before the first rep — there is no external load to do it for you.
targetNotes: Shift onto one leg, squatting as deep as mobility allows with the other leg straight out. Push back to centre.
trainerTip: Heel down on the working side is the goal — prop the heel if mobility says not yet.

name: Cross-Body Curl
setupNotes: Hold the dumbbells at your sides with neutral grips. Set the dumbbells within reach and plant your stance before you pick them up.
targetNotes: Curl one hand up and across to the opposite shoulder. Lower and alternate sides.
trainerTip: The diagonal path targets the long head and brachialis — smooth beats heavy.

name: Crunch
setupNotes: Lie on your back with the knees bent and hands by the ears. Brace hard before the first rep — there is no external load to do it for you.
targetNotes: Curl the shoulder blades off the floor, exhaling hard. Lower slowly, one vertebra at a time.
trainerTip: Curl the ribs toward the hips — pulling on the neck is banned.

name: Cuban Press
setupNotes: Hold light dumbbells at your sides with a neutral grip. Set the dumbbells within reach and plant your stance before you pick them up.
targetNotes: Raise the elbows to shoulder height, rotate the forearms up, then press overhead. Reverse the whole path down.
trainerTip: Very light and very strict — this builds the cuff that keeps your big presses healthy.

name: Curtsy Lunge
setupNotes: Stand tall holding weights at your sides. Set the dumbbells within reach and plant your stance before you pick them up.
targetNotes: Step one foot back and behind the other, lowering toward the floor. Return to standing under control.
trainerTip: It targets the glute medius — the stabiliser that keeps your knees honest.

name: Dead Bug
setupNotes: Lie on your back with the arms and knees up at 90° and the back flat. Brace hard before the first rep — there is no external load to do it for you.
targetNotes: Lower the opposite arm and leg toward the floor keeping the back glued down. Return and switch.
trainerTip: The lower back stays flat the entire time — that is the whole game.

name: Dead Hang
setupNotes: Grip the bar at shoulder width and step off into a full hang. Wipe the bar and set your grip width before you jump up.
targetNotes: Hang with straight arms and active shoulders for time. Keep your toes just off the floor.
trainerTip: A great finisher for grip and shoulder health — add time before adding weight.

name: Deadlift
setupNotes: Stand with the bar over mid-foot, shins a hand-width from the steel, and hinge down to grip. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Push the floor away keeping the bar dragging up your legs. Lock out tall with the glutes, not a lean-back.
trainerTip: The bar never leaves your legs — treat every millimetre of daylight as a technique fault.

name: Decline Barbell Bench Press
setupNotes: Lock your ankles under the pads and keep your hips planted on the decline bench. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Lower the weight to your lower chest on a controlled path. Press up through the same groove, thinking about the lower pec line.
trainerTip: The range is shorter than flat bench — recalibrate your warm-up weights before loading heavy.

name: Decline Cable Fly
setupNotes: Anchor your ankles and keep your hips down on the decline pad. Set the pulley height first, then test the travel with a light pin before loading.
targetNotes: Arc the weights out to chest level, then bring them together over the lower chest with elbows fixed.
trainerTip: Keep the range just inside the point where your shoulders roll forward.

name: Decline Crunch
setupNotes: Hook the ankles on a decline bench and lie back. Check the bench angle and anchor points before you set up.
targetNotes: Curl up into a full crunch against the angle. Lower with control to full extension.
trainerTip: The decline loads the abs in their longest position — control the descent like you mean it.

name: Decline Dumbbell Fly
setupNotes: Anchor your ankles and keep your hips down on the decline pad. Set the dumbbells within reach and plant your stance before you pick them up.
targetNotes: Arc the weights out to chest level, then bring them together over the lower chest with elbows fixed.
trainerTip: Keep the range just inside the point where your shoulders roll forward.

name: Decline Dumbbell Press
setupNotes: Lock your ankles under the pads and keep your hips planted on the decline bench. Set the dumbbells within reach and plant your stance before you pick them up.
targetNotes: Lower the weight to your lower chest on a controlled path. Press up through the same groove, thinking about the lower pec line.
trainerTip: The range is shorter than flat bench — recalibrate your warm-up weights before loading heavy.

name: Decline Push-Up
setupNotes: Set your feet on a box or bench and your hands slightly wider than shoulders. Set the box on a flat, non-slip surface before you start.
targetNotes: Lower your chest to the floor keeping the body in one line. Press up to lockout with the shoulders staying down.
trainerTip: The load shifts to upper chest and shoulders — cut the set when your lower back starts arching.

name: Decline Sit-Up
setupNotes: Hook the ankles at the top of a decline bench and lie back. Check the bench angle and anchor points before you set up.
targetNotes: Sit up the full way against the decline, then lower slowly to full extension.
trainerTip: The longer arc makes cheating harder — if the hands pull the neck, cross them over the chest.

name: Deficit Deadlift
setupNotes: Stand on a low plate or block with the bar in front of your shins. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Pull from the extra depth with the same flat-back wedge. Lock out tall on the platform.
trainerTip: Two inches of deficit is plenty — you are building range, not proving a point.

name: Diamond Push-Up
setupNotes: Form a diamond with your thumbs and index fingers under your chest. Brace hard before the first rep — there is no external load to do it for you.
targetNotes: Lower your chest onto your hands keeping the elbows tucked. Press to lockout.
trainerTip: The narrow hand position hammers the triceps — elevate the feet when it gets easy.

name: Donkey Calf Raise
setupNotes: Set the machine pad over your hips with the torso bent forward. Adjust the seat and handle height so the pad meets the working joint.
targetNotes: Stretch the heels down fully, then press to a peak contraction. Lower slowly.
trainerTip: The bent position stretches the calves at the hip — old-school and brutally effective.

name: Donkey Kick
setupNotes: Set up on all fours with the hands under the shoulders and a flat back. Brace hard before the first rep — there is no external load to do it for you.
targetNotes: Drive one heel toward the ceiling, squeezing the glute at the top. Return without letting the knee touch down.
trainerTip: Slow and squeezed — a flick of the foot trains nothing.

name: Double-Under
setupNotes: Size the rope to your sternum with one foot on its middle. Use a speed rope and keep the jump high while the wrists flick twice per hop.
targetNotes: Skip with small hops and the wrists doing the turning. Accumulate time or work in intervals.
trainerTip: Bounce off the balls of your feet — the floor is lava, softly.

name: Drag Curl
setupNotes: Hold the bar at arm's length with the elbows drawn back. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Drag the bar up your torso toward the chin keeping the elbows behind you. Lower down your body.
trainerTip: A small range with a huge squeeze — a finishing move, not a load move.

name: Dragon Flag
setupNotes: Grip the bench behind your head and drive the legs to vertical. Check the bench angle and anchor points before you set up.
targetNotes: Lower the whole body toward the bench as one rigid lever. Pull it back up with the core.
trainerTip: Bend at only one place — nowhere. Start with small lowers.

name: Dumbbell Bench Press
setupNotes: Lie back with your eyes just under the bar and drive your shoulder blades down and together. Set the dumbbells within reach and plant your stance before you pick them up.
targetNotes: Lower the weight to mid-chest with elbows about 45° from your torso. Press up and slightly back to lockout without losing the packed shoulders.
trainerTip: Grip wide enough that your forearms stay vertical at the bottom, and only use depth you can control every single rep.

name: Dumbbell Curl
setupNotes: Stand tall with the weight at arm's length and the elbows pinned to your ribs. Set the dumbbells within reach and plant your stance before you pick them up.
targetNotes: Curl to shoulder height without letting the elbows travel forward. Lower all the way to straight arms.
trainerTip: The elbows are hinges bolted to your sides — every inch they drift forward steals biceps.

name: Dumbbell Deadlift
setupNotes: Stand with the bar over mid-foot, shins a hand-width from the steel, and hinge down to grip. Set the dumbbells within reach and plant your stance before you pick them up.
targetNotes: Push the floor away keeping the bar dragging up your legs. Lock out tall with the glutes, not a lean-back.
trainerTip: The bar never leaves your legs — treat every millimetre of daylight as a technique fault.

name: Dumbbell Floor Press
setupNotes: Sit on the floor, press the weight to arm's length above your chest, then lie back and plant your feet. Set the dumbbells within reach and plant your stance before you pick them up.
targetNotes: Lower your elbows until they lightly touch the floor. Press up from that dead stop.
trainerTip: The dead stop kills the bounce — honest lockout strength for pressing sticking points.

name: Dumbbell Fly
setupNotes: Set your shoulders back and keep a soft, fixed bend in the elbows. Set the dumbbells within reach and plant your stance before you pick them up.
targetNotes: Open your arms in a wide arc until you feel a stretch across the chest. Squeeze the arms back together over mid-chest, not over your face.
trainerTip: Think of hugging a barrel — the arc does the work, not a press.

name: Dumbbell Front Squat
setupNotes: Clean or press two dumbbells to your shoulders with elbows high. Set the dumbbells within reach and plant your stance before you pick them up.
targetNotes: Squat to depth keeping the elbows up and the torso tall. Drive up through the whole foot.
trainerTip: A front-squat pattern without a bar — the dumbbells punish a collapsing chest instantly.

name: Dumbbell Goblet Squat
setupNotes: Hold the bell upside-down at your chest with elbows tucked inside the knees' path. Set the dumbbells within reach and plant your stance before you pick them up.
targetNotes: Squat between your hips to full depth keeping the chest tall. Stand squeezing the glutes at the top.
trainerTip: The counterweight lets beginners hit rock bottom safely — the best squat teacher there is.

name: Dumbbell Overhead Extension
setupNotes: Hold the weight overhead with both hands, elbows narrow and pointing forward. Set the dumbbells within reach and plant your stance before you pick them up.
targetNotes: Lower the weight behind your head by bending the elbows only. Extend to full lockout overhead.
trainerTip: The overhead position stretches the long head — the two-thirds of the triceps most lifts miss.

name: Dumbbell Preacher Curl
setupNotes: Set your armpits over the top of the pad with the arms stretched along it. Set the dumbbells within reach and plant your stance before you pick them up.
targetNotes: Curl to just under chin height. Lower to near-full extension without locking hard.
trainerTip: The pad forbids cheating — half-reps here are extra obvious, so do not.

name: Dumbbell Pullover
setupNotes: Lie along or across a bench holding one weight in both hands above your chest. Set the dumbbells within reach and plant your stance before you pick them up.
targetNotes: Lower the weight in an arc overhead until it levels with your head. Pull it back over your chest keeping the arms nearly straight.
trainerTip: Keep the ribs down — if your back arches to buy range, you have gone too far.

name: Dumbbell Push Press
setupNotes: Rack the bar as an overhead press with feet hip-width. Set the dumbbells within reach and plant your stance before you pick them up.
targetNotes: Dip a few inches, drive with the legs, and press overhead to finish. Lock out tall.
trainerTip: The legs start the press and the arms finish it — timing is the skill.

name: Dumbbell Reverse Wrist Curl
setupNotes: Rest your forearms on a bench with the wrists over the edge, palms down. Set the dumbbells within reach and plant your stance before you pick them up.
targetNotes: Lower the weight down, then raise the backs of your hands as high as they go.
trainerTip: The extensors balance all that gripping — elbow health insurance.

name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
setupNotes: Stand tall holding the weight with knees softly unlocked. Set the dumbbells within reach and plant your stance before you pick them up.
targetNotes: Push the hips back, lowering the weight down your thighs until the hamstrings max out. Stand by driving the hips forward, not lifting with the back.
trainerTip: It is a hamstring stretch with load — the moment your back rounds, the rep is over.

name: Dumbbell Row
setupNotes: Hinge to roughly 45° or flatter and brace your trunk before you touch the weight. Set the dumbbells within reach and plant your stance before you pick them up.
targetNotes: Drive your elbows back past your torso until the weight reaches your lower ribs. Lower under control to a full stretch without rounding.
trainerTip: Row with a still torso — if your hips pump, the load is writing cheques your back cannot cash.

name: Dumbbell Shoulder Press
setupNotes: Rack the bar on your front delts with elbows slightly ahead of it and feet hip-width. Set the dumbbells within reach and plant your stance before you pick them up.
targetNotes: Press the bar overhead, moving your head back as it passes, finishing with biceps by the ears. Lock out tall with the ribs down.
trainerTip: Squeeze the glutes and brace — a leaking midsection steals more press than weak shoulders do.

name: Dumbbell Shrug
setupNotes: Stand tall holding the weight with your shoulders pulled down and back. Set the dumbbells within reach and plant your stance before you pick them up.
targetNotes: Shrug your shoulders straight up toward your ears. Lower to a full stretch with control.
trainerTip: Straight up and straight down — rolling the shoulders adds injury risk, not growth.

name: Dumbbell Side Bend
setupNotes: Hold one dumbbell at your side with the other hand on your hip. Set the dumbbells within reach and plant your stance before you pick them up.
targetNotes: Bend sideways toward the weight, lowering it along the thigh. Pull back to tall with the opposite obliques.
trainerTip: One weight only — two weights cancel the whole point.

name: Dumbbell Skull Crusher
setupNotes: Lie on a bench holding the weight above your chest with arms roughly perpendicular to the floor. Set the dumbbells within reach and plant your stance before you pick them up.
targetNotes: Lower the weight behind your forehead by bending only the elbows. Extend back to straight arms.
trainerTip: The elbows stay put and point at the ceiling — flaring them forward shifts stress to the joints.

name: Dumbbell Snatch
setupNotes: Set one dumbbell between your feet and hinge with a flat back to grip it. Set the dumbbells within reach and plant your stance before you pick them up.
targetNotes: Explode from the floor and punch under, catching the bell overhead in one motion. Lower and reset.
trainerTip: Explosive hips, quiet catch — if the bell crashes onto the wrist, you flipped it late.

name: Dumbbell Squat
setupNotes: Set the bar across your traps, unrack, and take a stance just outside shoulder width. Set the dumbbells within reach and plant your stance before you pick them up.
targetNotes: Sit down between your hips until the hip crease passes the knee, or as deep as your back stays neutral. Drive up through mid-foot to stand tall.
trainerTip: Own the depth where you can keep a neutral spine — deeper at lighter load beats higher at max.

name: Dumbbell Squeeze Press
setupNotes: Press two dumbbells together over your chest with palms facing each other. Set the dumbbells within reach and plant your stance before you pick them up.
targetNotes: Keep squeezing the weights together as you lower to chest level. Press up while maintaining the squeeze the whole way.
trainerTip: The harder you squeeze, the more chest you get — a press and a fly disguised as one move.

name: Dumbbell Standing Calf Raise
setupNotes: Set the pads over your shoulders (or hold the weight) with the balls of your feet on the edge. Set the dumbbells within reach and plant your stance before you pick them up.
targetNotes: Drop the heels to a full stretch. Press up onto the toes as high as possible.
trainerTip: Pause one full second at the top and the bottom — bouncing is the calf-raise cheat code.

name: Dumbbell Stiff-Leg Deadlift
setupNotes: Set up as a deadlift, then stand with the knees nearly locked. Set the dumbbells within reach and plant your stance before you pick them up.
targetNotes: Hinge the bar down your shins to mid-shin or your lower-back tolerance. Pull to standing keeping the spine flat.
trainerTip: Stiffer knees shift the load lower into the hamstrings — respect the smaller margin for form.

name: Dumbbell Thruster
setupNotes: Hold two dumbbells at your shoulders with a squat-width stance. Set the dumbbells within reach and plant your stance before you pick them up.
targetNotes: Squat to depth, then drive the dumbbells overhead as you stand. Lower them back to the shoulders.
trainerTip: Lighter than the barbell version and friendlier to cranky shoulders.

name: Dumbbell Upright Row
setupNotes: Hold the weight in front of your thighs with an overhand grip. Set the dumbbells within reach and plant your stance before you pick them up.
targetNotes: Pull straight up to chest height keeping the elbows above the hands. Lower slowly.
trainerTip: Stop at chest height — pulling to the chin is where shoulders start complaining.

name: Dumbbell Wrist Curl
setupNotes: Rest your forearms on a bench with the wrists hanging over the edge, palms up. Set the dumbbells within reach and plant your stance before you pick them up.
targetNotes: Let the weight roll down to your fingertips, then curl it back up through full wrist flexion.
trainerTip: The full roller-coaster range — fingertips to full squeeze.

name: Dumbbell Y Raise
setupNotes: Lie chest-down on an incline bench with light dumbbells hanging. Set the dumbbells within reach and plant your stance before you pick them up.
targetNotes: Raise the arms out and overhead into a Y, thumbs up. Lower with control.
trainerTip: Very light weights, very high quality — lower-trap health for overhead pressing.

name: Elliptical
setupNotes: Step on and set the resistance and incline before you start pushing. Adjust the seat and handle height so the pad meets the working joint.
targetNotes: Move at the target effort with a full stride. Track distance and time.
trainerTip: A great low-impact alternative to running — keep the resistance honest though.

name: EZ-Bar Curl
setupNotes: Stand tall with the weight at arm's length and the elbows pinned to your ribs. Choose the grip groove that keeps your wrists neutral.
targetNotes: Curl to shoulder height without letting the elbows travel forward. Lower all the way to straight arms.
trainerTip: The elbows are hinges bolted to your sides — every inch they drift forward steals biceps.

name: EZ-Bar Overhead Extension
setupNotes: Hold the weight overhead with both hands, elbows narrow and pointing forward. Choose the grip groove that keeps your wrists neutral.
targetNotes: Lower the weight behind your head by bending the elbows only. Extend to full lockout overhead.
trainerTip: The overhead position stretches the long head — the two-thirds of the triceps most lifts miss.

name: EZ-Bar Skull Crusher
setupNotes: Lie on a bench holding the weight above your chest with arms roughly perpendicular to the floor. Choose the grip groove that keeps your wrists neutral.
targetNotes: Lower the weight behind your forehead by bending only the elbows. Extend back to straight arms.
trainerTip: The elbows stay put and point at the ceiling — flaring them forward shifts stress to the joints.

name: EZ-Bar Spider Curl
setupNotes: Set an incline bench steep and lie chest-down with the arms hanging straight. Choose the grip groove that keeps your wrists neutral.
targetNotes: Curl to shoulder height with zero elbow swing. Lower to a dead hang.
trainerTip: The strictest curl in the building — pick weights accordingly.

name: EZ-Bar Upright Row
setupNotes: Hold the weight in front of your thighs with an overhand grip. Choose the grip groove that keeps your wrists neutral.
targetNotes: Pull straight up to chest height keeping the elbows above the hands. Lower slowly.
trainerTip: Stop at chest height — pulling to the chin is where shoulders start complaining.

name: Face Pull
setupNotes: Set the rope at upper-chest height and step back into tension. Set the pulley height first, then test the travel with a light pin before loading.
targetNotes: Pull the rope toward your face, splitting the hands beside your ears. Return with control.
trainerTip: Finish with external rotation — posture insurance for desk-bound shoulders.

name: Farmer's Walk
setupNotes: Deadlift the weights to your sides and stand tall before the first step. Set the dumbbells within reach and plant your stance before you pick them up.
targetNotes: Walk with short, quick steps keeping the shoulders back and spine tall. Set the weights down only when the set ends.
trainerTip: Grip gives out before legs usually — chalk on, straps off, unless it is a dedicated grip day.

name: Fire Hydrant
setupNotes: Set up on all fours with a neutral spine and gaze down. Brace hard before the first rep — there is no external load to do it for you.
targetNotes: Lift one knee out to the side to hip height, keeping the bend fixed. Lower with control.
trainerTip: The thigh stays parallel to the floor — no rolling open at the hip to fake range.

name: Flutter Kick
setupNotes: Lie on your back with hands under the hips and legs hovering a few inches up. Brace hard before the first rep — there is no external load to do it for you.
targetNotes: Flutter the legs up and down in small, quick strokes with the lower back pressed flat.
trainerTip: Small strokes and a flat back — the legs never touch and the back never arches.

name: Forward Lunge
setupNotes: Stand tall with dumbbells at your sides. Set the dumbbells within reach and plant your stance before you pick them up.
targetNotes: Step forward, lowering the back knee toward the floor. Push back to standing through the front heel.
trainerTip: Control the landing — a crashing front foot means you stepped too far, too fast.

name: Front Raise
setupNotes: Stand tall holding the weights in front of your thighs. Set the dumbbells within reach and plant your stance before you pick them up.
targetNotes: Raise straight arms to shoulder height. Lower with control back to the thighs.
trainerTip: Front delts already work in every press — keep this volume small and deliberate.

name: Front Squat
setupNotes: Rack the bar on your front delts with elbows high and a grip just outside the shoulders. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Squat down keeping the elbows up and the torso vertical. Drive up staying tall through the chest.
trainerTip: Elbows dropping means the bar wants to roll — fix the position before adding plates.

name: Glute Bridge
setupNotes: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat and close to your hips. Brace hard before the first rep — there is no external load to do it for you.
targetNotes: Drive through the heels lifting the hips to a straight line. Squeeze the glutes at the top, then lower slowly.
trainerTip: Squeeze at the top like you are pinching a coin — two seconds minimum.

name: Glute-Ham Raise
setupNotes: Set your ankles under the pads with the thigh pad just above the knee. Set the gear up within reach so the set starts without scrambling.
targetNotes: Lower your body forward as one rigid line, then pull back up with the hamstrings and glutes. Use your hands to catch as needed.
trainerTip: The king of hamstring work — partial lowers build to full ones.

name: Goblet Squat
setupNotes: Hold the bell upside-down at your chest with elbows tucked inside the knees' path. Grip high on the handle and keep your wrist straight throughout.
targetNotes: Squat between your hips to full depth keeping the chest tall. Stand squeezing the glutes at the top.
trainerTip: The counterweight lets beginners hit rock bottom safely — the best squat teacher there is.

name: Good Morning
setupNotes: Set the bar on your traps as in a squat and unlock your knees slightly. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Hinge at the hips pushing them back until your torso approaches parallel. Drive the hips forward to stand tall.
trainerTip: Start with an empty bar for a week — this exercise rewards patience and punishes ego.

name: Gorilla Row
setupNotes: Set two bells between your feet, hinge over, and grip both handles. Grip high on the handle and keep your wrist straight throughout.
targetNotes: Row one bell to your hip while the other stays hanging. Alternate sides with a still torso.
trainerTip: Anti-rotation is the secret — your obliques work as hard as your lats.

name: Hack Squat
setupNotes: Load the sled and set your back against the pad with shoulders under the yoke. Adjust the seat and handle height so the pad meets the working joint.
targetNotes: Descend until your thighs approach parallel. Drive up through the heels without slamming into lockout.
trainerTip: The machine stabilises you, so make up for it by chasing full depth.

name: Hammer Curl
setupNotes: Hold the weights with a neutral grip — palms facing in — at your sides. Set the dumbbells within reach and plant your stance before you pick them up.
targetNotes: Curl straight up keeping the palms facing each other throughout. Lower fully.
trainerTip: Hits the brachialis that pushes the biceps up — pair it with regular curls.

name: Handstand Push-Up
setupNotes: Kick up to a wall with hands shoulder-width and the body stacked. Brace hard before the first rep — there is no external load to do it for you.
targetNotes: Lower your head to the floor between your hands. Press back to full lockout.
trainerTip: Partial reps with full control beat crashes — scale the range with mats.

name: Hang Power Clean
setupNotes: Stand tall holding the bar, then hinge it to just above your knees. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Explode from the hang position, catching the bar on your shoulders with elbows high. Reset above the knee every rep.
trainerTip: The hang version teaches the second pull — bar-path discipline without the floor start.

name: Hanging Knee Raise
setupNotes: Hang from the bar with a grip you can hold for the whole set. Wipe the bar and set your grip width before you jump up.
targetNotes: Drive the knees toward the chest, curling the hips up. Lower to a dead hang without swinging.
trainerTip: Curl the pelvis at the top — lifting the knees alone is a hip-flexor holiday.

name: Hanging Leg Raise
setupNotes: Hang from the bar with an overhand grip and a still body. Wipe the bar and set your grip width before you jump up.
targetNotes: Raise straight legs to horizontal or higher using the abs, not a swing. Lower slowly.
trainerTip: Bend the knees if straight legs make you swing — a strict knee raise beats a flailing leg raise.

name: High Knees
setupNotes: Stand tall with the elbows bent at your sides. Brace hard before the first rep — there is no external load to do it for you.
targetNotes: Jog in place driving the knees to hip height with a quick, tall posture.
trainerTip: Punch the ground with short ground contacts — the hips stay high, never sitting back.

name: Hill Sprints
setupNotes: Pick a hill with a safe, clear slope and warm up at the bottom. Brace hard before the first rep — there is no external load to do it for you.
targetNotes: Sprint up the hill with powerful strides, then walk down to recover. Repeat for the planned reps.
trainerTip: The hill forces good mechanics — a natural speed limiter for the ego.

name: Hip Abduction
setupNotes: Set the machine pads against your outer thighs and sit square. Adjust the seat and handle height so the pad meets the working joint.
targetNotes: Press your legs outward to your full pain-free range. Return slowly without letting the weight slam.
trainerTip: Glute medius is the knee's bodyguard — do not skip it just because the loads look small.

name: Hip Adduction
setupNotes: Set the pads against your inner thighs and sit square to the machine. Adjust the seat and handle height so the pad meets the working joint.
targetNotes: Draw your legs together through the full range. Return with control.
trainerTip: Groin health insurance — especially if your sport changes direction.

name: Hip Thrust
setupNotes: Set your upper back on a bench with the barbell padded over your hips and feet planted. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Drive the hips to full lockout with the chin tucked and ribs down. Lower to a hover and repeat.
trainerTip: Chin tucked and eyes forward — a lifted chin borrows from the glutes and hands the change to the lower back.

name: Hollow Body Hold
setupNotes: Lie flat with the arms overhead and legs straight. Brace hard before the first rep — there is no external load to do it for you.
targetNotes: Press the lower back into the floor and lift the shoulders and legs into a banana shape. Hold for time.
trainerTip: Shorten the lever — arms by the sides or knees tucked — before letting the back arch.

name: Hyperextension
setupNotes: Set the pad at your hip crease and anchor your ankles. Brace hard before the first rep — there is no external load to do it for you.
targetNotes: Hinge down over the pad to a comfortable hamstring stretch. Rise until your body forms one straight line, no higher.
trainerTip: Stop at straight — hyperextending the back buys nothing but a sore tomorrow.

name: Incline Barbell Bench Press
setupNotes: Set the bench to a 30–45° angle and plant your feet firmly on the floor. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Lower the weight to your upper chest, keeping elbows under the wrists. Press up in a slight arc toward eye level.
trainerTip: Stop the set when your shoulders creep up toward your ears — that is the incline stealing your press.

name: Incline Cable Fly
setupNotes: Set the bench to 30–45° and pin your shoulder blades to the pad. Set the pulley height first, then test the travel with a light pin before loading.
targetNotes: Arc the arms out until they level with your torso. Sweep them up and together over the upper chest with the same elbow bend throughout.
trainerTip: Go lighter than your flat fly — the stretched position at the top of the arc is the risk point.

name: Incline Dumbbell Curl
setupNotes: Lie back on a 45–60° bench with the arms hanging straight down. Set the dumbbells within reach and plant your stance before you pick them up.
targetNotes: Curl up without letting the elbows swing forward. Lower to the full hang stretch.
trainerTip: The stretch position is the magic — do not shorten it to lift heavier.

name: Incline Dumbbell Fly
setupNotes: Set the bench to 30–45° and pin your shoulder blades to the pad. Set the dumbbells within reach and plant your stance before you pick them up.
targetNotes: Arc the arms out until they level with your torso. Sweep them up and together over the upper chest with the same elbow bend throughout.
trainerTip: Go lighter than your flat fly — the stretched position at the top of the arc is the risk point.

name: Incline Dumbbell Press
setupNotes: Set the bench to a 30–45° angle and plant your feet firmly on the floor. Set the dumbbells within reach and plant your stance before you pick them up.
targetNotes: Lower the weight to your upper chest, keeping elbows under the wrists. Press up in a slight arc toward eye level.
trainerTip: Stop the set when your shoulders creep up toward your ears — that is the incline stealing your press.

name: Incline Dumbbell Row
setupNotes: Set an incline bench to 30–45° and lie chest-down with the dumbbells hanging. Set the dumbbells within reach and plant your stance before you pick them up.
targetNotes: Row the weights to your ribs keeping the chest on the pad. Lower to a full stretch.
trainerTip: Chest support deletes the torso swing — the honest row for heavy days.

name: Incline Hammer Curl
setupNotes: Lie back on a 45–60° bench with neutral-grip dumbbells hanging. Set the dumbbells within reach and plant your stance before you pick them up.
targetNotes: Hammer-curl up from the stretched position without elbow swing. Lower to the full hang.
trainerTip: The stretched start plus neutral grip lights up the brachialis — slow the negatives down.

name: Incline Machine Press
setupNotes: Set the bench to a 30–45° angle and plant your feet firmly on the floor. Adjust the seat and handle height so the pad meets the working joint.
targetNotes: Lower the weight to your upper chest, keeping elbows under the wrists. Press up in a slight arc toward eye level.
trainerTip: Stop the set when your shoulders creep up toward your ears — that is the incline stealing your press.

name: Incline Push-Up
setupNotes: Place your hands on a stable elevated surface at roughly knee-to-hip height. Set the box on a flat, non-slip surface before you start.
targetNotes: Lower your chest to the edge with a rigid torso. Press back to straight arms without letting the hips drop.
trainerTip: Higher is easier — pick an angle where you can own ten clean reps before progressing lower.

name: Incline Rear Delt Fly
setupNotes: Hinge to 45° or rest chest-down on an incline bench with the weights hanging. Set the dumbbells within reach and plant your stance before you pick them up.
targetNotes: Raise the arms out to the sides with a soft elbow bend, squeezing the shoulder blades. Lower slowly.
trainerTip: Lead with the pinkies and think 'thumbs up' — it is a fly, not a row.

name: Incline Treadmill Walk
setupNotes: Set the belt speed and incline before you step on. Set the incline to 8–12% and keep the speed honest enough to need it.
targetNotes: Walk at your target pace with a tall posture, hands off the rails. Track distance and time.
trainerTip: Crank the incline before the speed — a steep walk rivals a slow jog for effort.

name: Inverted Row
setupNotes: Set a bar at hip height in a rack and hang beneath it with straight arms. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Pull your chest to the bar keeping your body rigid from heels to head. Lower to straight arms without the hips sagging.
trainerTip: Walk your feet forward to make it harder — no plates required.

name: JM Press
setupNotes: Lie on a bench with a close grip and the bar over your chest. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Lower toward your neck, bending the elbows and letting them travel slightly back. Extend back to above your chest.
trainerTip: Half skull-crusher, half close-grip press — start light, it finds the elbows fast.

name: Jump Rope
setupNotes: Size the rope to your sternum with one foot on its middle. Set the gear up within reach so the set starts without scrambling.
targetNotes: Skip with small hops and the wrists doing the turning. Accumulate time or work in intervals.
trainerTip: Bounce off the balls of your feet — the floor is lava, softly.

name: Jump Squat
setupNotes: Set your squat stance with no load or a very light bar. Brace hard before the first rep — there is no external load to do it for you.
targetNotes: Drop to a quarter squat and jump as high as possible. Absorb the landing into your next rep.
trainerTip: Maximum intent on every rep — power training at half speed trains nothing.

name: Jumping Jack
setupNotes: Stand with the feet together and arms at the sides. Brace hard before the first rep — there is no external load to do it for you.
targetNotes: Jump the feet wide while raising the arms overhead. Jump back to the start and keep the rhythm.
trainerTip: A warm-up classic — also great between strength sets to stay warm.

name: Jumping Lunge
setupNotes: Drop into a lunge with your torso tall and arms ready to swing. Brace hard before the first rep — there is no external load to do it for you.
targetNotes: Switch legs mid-air, landing each rep in a full lunge. Absorb the landings with soft knees.
trainerTip: Land quiet — noise is wasted power leaking out.

name: Kettlebell Bottom-Up Press
setupNotes: Clean the bell upside-down so the flat bottom faces the ceiling, elbow under the handle. Grip high on the handle and keep your wrist straight throughout.
targetNotes: Press overhead keeping the bell stacked vertical. Lower with the same focus.
trainerTip: The imbalance lights up the rotator cuff — start with a bell half your usual press weight.

name: Kettlebell Clean
setupNotes: Set the bell a shoe-length in front of you, hinge, and grip one-handed. Grip high on the handle and keep your wrist straight throughout.
targetNotes: Hike the bell back and snap the hips, catching it softly in the front rack. Drop and re-hinge between reps.
trainerTip: The catch should land like a handshake, not a punch — taming the arc is the skill.

name: Kettlebell Clean and Press
setupNotes: Set the bell one shoe-length ahead and hinge with one hand on the handle. Grip high on the handle and keep your wrist straight throughout.
targetNotes: Clean the bell to the rack, then press it overhead. Lower and re-hike for the next rep.
trainerTip: One smooth chain from floor to lockout — the reps should look identical from first to last.

name: Kettlebell Farmer's Walk
setupNotes: Deadlift the weights to your sides and stand tall before the first step. Grip high on the handle and keep your wrist straight throughout.
targetNotes: Walk with short, quick steps keeping the shoulders back and spine tall. Set the weights down only when the set ends.
trainerTip: Grip gives out before legs usually — chalk on, straps off, unless it is a dedicated grip day.

name: Kettlebell Floor Press
setupNotes: Lie on the floor and press the bells to arm's length above your chest. Grip high on the handle and keep your wrist straight throughout.
targetNotes: Lower the elbows to lightly touch the floor. Press up from the dead stop each rep.
trainerTip: The floor caps the range — pure lockout pressing with a wrist-stability side order.

name: Kettlebell Front Rack Carry
setupNotes: Clean one or two bells to the front rack — elbows tucked, wrists straight. Grip high on the handle and keep your wrist straight throughout.
targetNotes: Walk with a tall spine and locked ribcage, keeping the bells pinned to the chest. Set them down only when the set ends.
trainerTip: The rack position trains the core and upper back at once — quiet breathing is the advanced skill.

name: Kettlebell Front Squat
setupNotes: Clean two bells to the front rack with elbows tucked tight to the ribs. Grip high on the handle and keep your wrist straight throughout.
targetNotes: Squat between the bells to full depth keeping the chest proud. Stand squeezing the glutes.
trainerTip: The double rack makes the abs work overtime — a squat wearing a weighted vest.

name: Kettlebell Halo
setupNotes: Hold the bell by the horn upside-down at your chest, elbows down. Grip high on the handle and keep your wrist straight throughout.
targetNotes: Circle the bell around your head one way, keeping the ribs stacked. Reverse the direction each set.
trainerTip: A mobility drill with load — tight shoulders loosen and the core learns to stay still.

name: Kettlebell Overhead Press
