setupNotes: Rack the bar on your front delts with elbows slightly ahead of it and feet hip-width. Grip high on the handle and keep your wrist straight throughout.
targetNotes: Press the bar overhead, moving your head back as it passes, finishing with biceps by the ears. Lock out tall with the ribs down.
trainerTip: Squeeze the glutes and brace — a leaking midsection steals more press than weak shoulders do.

name: Kettlebell Row
setupNotes: Set the bell beside a bench, brace one hand and knee on the bench, and flatten your back. Grip high on the handle and keep your wrist straight throughout.
targetNotes: Row the bell to your hip keeping the elbow tight to your side. Lower to a full hang without twisting your torso.
trainerTip: Pause at the top for a beat — chasing the burn with swings turns it into a hip hinge.

name: Kettlebell Seesaw Press
setupNotes: Clean two bells to the rack with elbows tucked. Grip high on the handle and keep your wrist straight throughout.
targetNotes: Press one bell overhead while the other stays racked, then alternate in a steady seesaw.
trainerTip: Constant rack tension makes the abs and lats co-sign every press.

name: Kettlebell Single-Leg RDL
setupNotes: Hold the weight on one side and stand on the opposite leg. Grip high on the handle and keep your wrist straight throughout.
targetNotes: Hinge forward on one leg with the free leg extending behind you. Feel the working hamstring load, then stand tall.
trainerTip: Slow beats heavy — a wobbly single-leg RDL trains nothing but excuses.

name: Kettlebell Snatch
setupNotes: Set the bell one shoe-length ahead and hinge with one hand on the handle. Grip high on the handle and keep your wrist straight throughout.
targetNotes: Hike and explode, punching your hand through as the bell flips over the wrist to overhead lockout. Lower and re-hike.
trainerTip: Punch through, never flip-and-catch — the bruised-forearm version is the one you skip.

name: Kettlebell Sumo Squat
setupNotes: Stand wide with toes out, holding the bell by the horn at your chest. Grip high on the handle and keep your wrist straight throughout.
targetNotes: Sit straight down between your hips to full depth, then drive up pressing the knees out.
trainerTip: The bell's hang counterbalances the wide stance — go deep, stay tall.

name: Kettlebell Swing
setupNotes: Set the bell one shoe-length in front of you, hinge, and grip with both hands. Grip high on the handle and keep your wrist straight throughout.
targetNotes: Hike the bell back between your legs, then snap the hips forward to swing it to chest height. Let it fall and re-hinge.
trainerTip: It is a hinge, not a squat, and a hip snap, not an arm lift — the bell floats up on momentum.

name: Kettlebell Walking Lunge
setupNotes: Stand tall with the weight held at your sides or in the front rack. Grip high on the handle and keep your wrist straight throughout.
targetNotes: Step forward and lower until the back knee hovers at the floor. Push through the front leg to step into the next rep.
trainerTip: Long steps bias the glutes and short steps the quads — choose on purpose.

name: Kettlebell Windmill
setupNotes: Press the bell overhead and set your feet angled away from the working side. Grip high on the handle and keep your wrist straight throughout.
targetNotes: Hinge and rotate sideways, sliding the free hand down your leg toward the floor. Stand tall keeping the bell stacked.
trainerTip: Eyes on the bell the whole way down — the obliques write this cheque.

name: Knee Push-Up
setupNotes: Set hands just outside shoulder width and lower the knees to the floor behind the hips. Brace hard before the first rep — there is no external load to do it for you.
targetNotes: Lower the chest to a fist off the floor with a straight line from knees to head. Press back to lockout.
trainerTip: The on-ramp to full push-ups — graduate when ten clean reps feel easy.

name: L-Sit
setupNotes: Support yourself between parallettes or on the floor with the hands by your hips. Brace hard before the first rep — there is no external load to do it for you.
targetNotes: Lift and hold straight legs at hip height with locked arms. Hold for time.
trainerTip: One-leg or tucked holds build toward the full L — earn it in stages.

name: Landmine Press
setupNotes: Load one end of a bar in a landmine and hold the sleeve at shoulder height. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Press up and forward along the bar's natural arc to extension. Lower with control.
trainerTip: The angled path spares cranky shoulders while pressing hard — a rehab-room hero.

name: Landmine Squat
setupNotes: Load one end of a bar in a landmine and hold the sleeve at your chest. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Squat down keeping the bar angled in front of you and the torso upright. Stand tall.
trainerTip: The front-loaded angle spares the back and knees — friendly depth for big legs.

name: Landmine Twist
setupNotes: Hold the bar sleeve at chest height with the bar anchored in a landmine. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Rotate the bar end from hip to hip, pivoting through the ribs. Move with control.
trainerTip: Fast rotations wreck the low back — this one owns its tempo.

name: Lat Pulldown
setupNotes: Seat yourself with thighs locked under the pads and take an overhand grip just outside shoulder width. Set the pulley height first, then test the travel with a light pin before loading.
targetNotes: Pull the bar to your upper chest driving the elbows down and back. Let the bar rise until your lats fully stretch.
trainerTip: Lead with the elbows — your hands are hooks and your armpits do the pulling.

name: Lateral Raise
setupNotes: Stand tall with the weights at your sides and a slight forward lean. Set the dumbbells within reach and plant your stance before you pick them up.
targetNotes: Raise the arms out to shoulder height leading with the elbows. Lower slowly — no free fall.
trainerTip: Light weight and honest reps; think of a tiny forward tilt at the top like pouring water.

name: Leg Extension
setupNotes: Set the pad just above your ankles and adjust the seat back. Adjust the seat and handle height so the pad meets the working joint.
targetNotes: Extend to a full lockout and squeeze the quad for a beat. Lower under control, never dropping the stack.
trainerTip: Pause at the top — riding the machine's momentum is why legs do not grow.

name: Leg Press
setupNotes: Set your back flat on the seat with feet shoulder-width on the platform. Adjust the seat and handle height so the pad meets the working joint.
targetNotes: Lower the sled until the knees reach your chest without the hips rolling up. Press to just short of locked knees.
trainerTip: Butt lifting off the seat at the bottom means the range is too big for today — back the depth off.

name: Leg Press Calf Raise
setupNotes: Set your feet on the top edge of the leg press platform with the balls of your feet on it. Adjust the seat and handle height so the pad meets the working joint.
targetNotes: Press the platform out to just short of knee lock, then drop the heels to a full stretch. Press up onto the toes.
trainerTip: The leg press lets you load the calves heavily — still honour the pause at both ends.

name: Lying Leg Curl
setupNotes: Lie face-down with the pad just above your heels and hips pressed into the bench. Adjust the seat and handle height so the pad meets the working joint.
targetNotes: Curl your heels toward your glutes. Lower to near-full extension without letting the hips pop up.
trainerTip: Hips glued down — lifting them is the machine's invitation to cheat.

name: Lying Leg Raise
setupNotes: Lie on your back with the hands under the hips for support. Brace hard before the first rep — there is no external load to do it for you.
targetNotes: Raise straight legs to vertical keeping the lower back flat. Lower to a hover, not the floor.
trainerTip: Stop an inch off the floor — that is where the abs live.

name: Machine Back Extension
setupNotes: Adjust the pad height so it meets your shoulder blades while seated side-on. Adjust the seat and handle height so the pad meets the working joint.
targetNotes: Hinge back against the pad extending the spine. Return forward under control.
trainerTip: Squeeze at extension and never bounce — the machine makes cheating tempting.

name: Machine Chest Press
setupNotes: Lie back with your eyes just under the bar and drive your shoulder blades down and together. Adjust the seat and handle height so the pad meets the working joint.
targetNotes: Lower the weight to mid-chest with elbows about 45° from your torso. Press up and slightly back to lockout without losing the packed shoulders.
trainerTip: Grip wide enough that your forearms stay vertical at the bottom, and only use depth you can control every single rep.

name: Machine Crunch
setupNotes: Lie on your back with the knees bent and hands by the ears. Adjust the seat and handle height so the pad meets the working joint.
targetNotes: Curl the shoulder blades off the floor, exhaling hard. Lower slowly, one vertebra at a time.
trainerTip: Curl the ribs toward the hips — pulling on the neck is banned.

name: Machine Curl
setupNotes: Stand tall with the weight at arm's length and the elbows pinned to your ribs. Adjust the seat and handle height so the pad meets the working joint.
targetNotes: Curl to shoulder height without letting the elbows travel forward. Lower all the way to straight arms.
trainerTip: The elbows are hinges bolted to your sides — every inch they drift forward steals biceps.

name: Machine Hip Thrust
setupNotes: Set your upper back on a bench with the barbell padded over your hips and feet planted. Adjust the seat and handle height so the pad meets the working joint.
targetNotes: Drive the hips to full lockout with the chin tucked and ribs down. Lower to a hover and repeat.
trainerTip: Chin tucked and eyes forward — a lifted chin borrows from the glutes and hands the change to the lower back.

name: Machine Lateral Raise
setupNotes: Stand tall with the weights at your sides and a slight forward lean. Adjust the seat and handle height so the pad meets the working joint.
targetNotes: Raise the arms out to shoulder height leading with the elbows. Lower slowly — no free fall.
trainerTip: Light weight and honest reps; think of a tiny forward tilt at the top like pouring water.

name: Machine Preacher Curl
setupNotes: Set your armpits over the top of the pad with the arms stretched along it. Adjust the seat and handle height so the pad meets the working joint.
targetNotes: Curl to just under chin height. Lower to near-full extension without locking hard.
trainerTip: The pad forbids cheating — half-reps here are extra obvious, so do not.

name: Machine Pullover
setupNotes: Set the seat so the pad sits against your forearms and the path clears your torso. Adjust the seat and handle height so the pad meets the working joint.
targetNotes: Pull the pad down and back through a wide arc until it touches your thighs. Return to a full stretch overhead.
trainerTip: Straight arms and a big arc — think of it as a lat pulldown lying down.

name: Machine Row
setupNotes: Hinge to roughly 45° or flatter and brace your trunk before you touch the weight. Adjust the seat and handle height so the pad meets the working joint.
targetNotes: Drive your elbows back past your torso until the weight reaches your lower ribs. Lower under control to a full stretch without rounding.
trainerTip: Row with a still torso — if your hips pump, the load is writing cheques your back cannot cash.

name: Machine Shoulder Press
setupNotes: Rack the bar on your front delts with elbows slightly ahead of it and feet hip-width. Adjust the seat and handle height so the pad meets the working joint.
targetNotes: Press the bar overhead, moving your head back as it passes, finishing with biceps by the ears. Lock out tall with the ribs down.
trainerTip: Squeeze the glutes and brace — a leaking midsection steals more press than weak shoulders do.

name: Machine Shrug
setupNotes: Stand tall holding the weight with your shoulders pulled down and back. Adjust the seat and handle height so the pad meets the working joint.
targetNotes: Shrug your shoulders straight up toward your ears. Lower to a full stretch with control.
trainerTip: Straight up and straight down — rolling the shoulders adds injury risk, not growth.

name: Machine Triceps Extension
setupNotes: Face a high pulley with the straight bar attached and elbows pinned to your sides. Adjust the seat and handle height so the pad meets the working joint.
targetNotes: Extend to straight arms keeping the upper arms still. Let the weight return to a controlled 90°.
trainerTip: Pin the elbows — if they drift forward, the chest and lats start freelancing.

name: Machine-Assisted Dip
setupNotes: Kneel or stand on the assist pad with a counterweight selected and grip the handles. Adjust the seat and handle height so the pad meets the working joint.
targetNotes: Lower until the elbows reach about 90°, letting the machine offset part of your weight. Press to lockout.
trainerTip: Trim the assistance plate as dips get easier — same progression ladder as the pull-up.

name: Machine-Assisted Pull-Up
setupNotes: Kneel on the pad and select an assistance weight that counters part of your bodyweight. Adjust the seat and handle height so the pad meets the working joint.
targetNotes: Pull your chin over the grips with the machine offsetting some load. Lower to full arms with control.
trainerTip: Cut the assistance pin by one plate when the reps get easy — steady progression out.

name: Meadows Row
setupNotes: Load one end of a bar in a landmine and stand parallel to it in a staggered stance. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Row the sleeve-end toward your lower ribs with a supinated grip. Lower slowly, letting the shoulder blade ride forward.
trainerTip: Let the shoulder blade move — the extra stretch at the bottom is the whole point.

name: Medicine Ball Chest Throw
setupNotes: Stand square to a solid wall a pace away with the ball held at chest height. Choose a ball weight you can move fast or hold with control.
targetNotes: Throw the ball sharply at the wall, extending through the elbows. Catch the rebound and absorb it back to your chest.
trainerTip: Throw with intent — power work only works at full speed.

name: Medicine Ball Sit-Up
setupNotes: Bend the knees, anchor the feet lightly, and set the hands by the ears. Choose a ball weight you can move fast or hold with control.
targetNotes: Sit all the way up to a tall torso. Lower under control until the shoulder blades touch.
trainerTip: If your feet fly up, cross the arms over the chest or brace them under a bench.

name: Medicine Ball Slam
setupNotes: Stand tall holding the ball overhead with straight arms. Choose a ball weight you can move fast or hold with control.
targetNotes: Slam the ball into the floor with full intent, hinging through the core. Catch the rebound or pick it clean.
trainerTip: Every slam is a full-body sprint — a dead ball is a wasted rep.

name: Mountain Climbers
setupNotes: Set a push-up position with the hands under the shoulders. Brace hard before the first rep — there is no external load to do it for you.
targetNotes: Drive the knees toward the chest, alternating quickly while the hips stay level.
trainerTip: Hips low and still — the legs sprint while the torso plays statue.

name: Mountain Hiking
setupNotes: Pack water and check the route and weather before you set out. Brace hard before the first rep — there is no external load to do it for you.
targetNotes: Walk the trail at a sustainable effort — poles if it is steep. Track distance and time.
trainerTip: Downhills are the quad tax — short steps and bent knees on the way home.

name: Negative Pull-Up
setupNotes: Stand or jump to the top position with the chin over the bar. Wipe the bar and set your grip width before you jump up.
targetNotes: Lower yourself to a dead hang as slowly as you can manage — five full seconds is gold. Reset to the top each rep.
trainerTip: Eccentric-only builds the strength for the full pull-up — the slow reps count double.

name: Neutral-Grip Pull-Up
setupNotes: Hang from parallel grips with palms facing each other. Wipe the bar and set your grip width before you jump up.
targetNotes: Pull until your chin passes your hands. Lower all the way to a dead hang.
trainerTip: The neutral grip lets lats move through their biggest range — great for heavy added weight.

name: Nordic Curl
setupNotes: Anchor your ankles under a pad or a partner's grip and kneel tall. Brace hard before the first rep — there is no external load to do it for you.
targetNotes: Lower your body forward as one rigid line as far as the hamstrings allow. Catch with your hands and pull back up.
trainerTip: Even a 20cm lowering is a legit set — the eccentric counts here.

name: Outdoor Cycling
setupNotes: Check the brakes and tyre pressure, and buckle the helmet. Set the saddle height so your knee keeps a slight bend at the bottom of the stroke.
targetNotes: Ride the planned route or distance. Track distance and time.
trainerTip: A cadence around 85–95 rpm spares the knees and lets the engine do the work.

name: Overhead Barbell Extension
setupNotes: Hold the weight overhead with both hands, elbows narrow and pointing forward. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Lower the weight behind your head by bending the elbows only. Extend to full lockout overhead.
trainerTip: The overhead position stretches the long head — the two-thirds of the triceps most lifts miss.

name: Overhead Cable Extension
setupNotes: Hold the weight overhead with both hands, elbows narrow and pointing forward. Set the pulley height first, then test the travel with a light pin before loading.
targetNotes: Lower the weight behind your head by bending the elbows only. Extend to full lockout overhead.
trainerTip: The overhead position stretches the long head — the two-thirds of the triceps most lifts miss.

name: Overhead Press
setupNotes: Rack the bar on your front delts with elbows slightly ahead of it and feet hip-width. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Press the bar overhead, moving your head back as it passes, finishing with biceps by the ears. Lock out tall with the ribs down.
trainerTip: Squeeze the glutes and brace — a leaking midsection steals more press than weak shoulders do.

name: Overhead Squat
setupNotes: Press or snatch a bar overhead with a wide grip and lock the shoulders in. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Squat to full depth keeping the bar stacked over mid-foot. Stand keeping the arms locked throughout.
trainerTip: Start with an empty bar — this is a mobility and balance test before it is a strength move.

name: Pallof Press
setupNotes: Stand side-on to a cable at chest height holding the handle at the sternum. Set the pulley height first, then test the travel with a light pin before loading.
targetNotes: Press the handle straight out, resisting the twist. Hold, return, and keep the ribs square.
trainerTip: The anti-rotation squeeze is the rep — if you are rotating, you are just pressing air.

name: Pause Squat
setupNotes: Set up as your normal squat with a weight you can control in the hole. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Descend, freeze the bottom position for a full two-count, then drive up with no bounce.
trainerTip: The drive out of a dead stop is where squat strength is actually built.

name: Pec Deck Fly
setupNotes: Set the seat so the pads line up with mid-chest and the range limiter matches your shoulder width. Adjust the seat and handle height so the pad meets the working joint.
targetNotes: Bring the pads together in front of your chest with a slight forward lean. Return until your arms level with your torso, and no further.
trainerTip: Elbows just below shoulder height keeps the stress on the pecs instead of the shoulder joint.

name: Pendlay Row
setupNotes: Set your torso parallel to the floor over the bar with arms hanging straight. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Snatch the bar to your sternum in one explosive pull. Return it to the floor and reset dead-stop every rep.
trainerTip: Every rep starts from the floor — that is what separates it from a regular row.

name: Pike Push-Up
setupNotes: From push-up position, walk your feet in and lift the hips high into an A-frame. Brace hard before the first rep — there is no external load to do it for you.
targetNotes: Lower the crown of your head toward the floor between your hands. Press back to the A-frame.
trainerTip: Elevate your feet to dial it up — a home shoulder press in disguise.

name: Pistol Squat
setupNotes: Stand on one leg with the other extended forward. Brace hard before the first rep — there is no external load to do it for you.
targetNotes: Sit down to full depth on one leg keeping the free leg high. Stand back up under control.
trainerTip: Build up with box pistols — the full version arrives when it is earned.

name: Plank
setupNotes: Set the elbows under the shoulders and step the feet back into one straight line. Brace hard before the first rep — there is no external load to do it for you.
targetNotes: Hold the line — ribs down, glutes on — for time. Breathe shallow and steady.
trainerTip: A straight line, not a tent or a hammock — quality over clock.

name: Plank Jacks
setupNotes: Set a forearm plank with the body in one line. Brace hard before the first rep — there is no external load to do it for you.
targetNotes: Jump the feet out wide and back together, keeping the hips level throughout.
trainerTip: The hips are the metronome — if they bounce, slow the tempo.

name: Plank Shoulder Taps
setupNotes: Set a plank with the hands under the shoulders and feet wide for stability. Brace hard before the first rep — there is no external load to do it for you.
targetNotes: Lift one hand and tap the opposite shoulder without letting the hips sway. Alternate with control.
trainerTip: Widen the feet to fight the wobble — still hips are the whole rep.

name: Plate Front Raise
setupNotes: Stand tall holding the weights in front of your thighs. Pick a plate you can hold securely for the whole set.
targetNotes: Raise straight arms to shoulder height. Lower with control back to the thighs.
trainerTip: Front delts already work in every press — keep this volume small and deliberate.

name: Plate Pinch
setupNotes: Pinch two smooth plates together between your fingers and thumb. Pick a plate you can hold securely for the whole set.
targetNotes: Hold the pinch for time, or walk small steps with the plates pinched.
trainerTip: Thumb strength drives the pinch — do not let the fingers do all the work.

name: Power Clean
setupNotes: Set up like a deadlift with the bar over mid-foot and a grip just outside shoulder width. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Explode the bar up and whip the elbows under to catch it on your shoulders. Stand tall, then lower and reset.
trainerTip: Spend your first month on light technique — power cleans reward precision more than grit.

name: Power Snatch
setupNotes: Grip snatch-wide and set a tall chest over the bar. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Drive the bar overhead in one motion, punching under to lock it out. Lower with control and reset.
trainerTip: Start with a dowel or empty bar — this is the most technical lift in the book.

name: Preacher Curl
setupNotes: Set your armpits over the top of the pad with the arms stretched along it. Choose the grip groove that keeps your wrists neutral.
targetNotes: Curl to just under chin height. Lower to near-full extension without locking hard.
trainerTip: The pad forbids cheating — half-reps here are extra obvious, so do not.

name: Pull-Up
setupNotes: Hang from the bar with an overhand grip just outside shoulder width. Wipe the bar and set your grip width before you jump up.
targetNotes: Pull until your chin clears the bar, driving the elbows to your ribs. Lower to a dead hang with straight arms every rep.
trainerTip: Full dead hang, full clearance — half reps build half a back.

name: Push Jerk
setupNotes: Front-rack the bar with feet hip-width. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Dip and drive, then drop under the bar, catching it overhead with bent knees. Stand tall with it locked out.
trainerTip: The second dip is the trick — you receive the bar lower instead of pressing it higher.

name: Push Press
setupNotes: Rack the bar as an overhead press with feet hip-width. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Dip a few inches, drive with the legs, and press overhead to finish. Lock out tall.
trainerTip: The legs start the press and the arms finish it — timing is the skill.

name: Push-Up
setupNotes: Set hands just outside shoulder width and step your feet back into one straight line. Brace hard before the first rep — there is no external load to do it for you.
targetNotes: Lower until your chest is a fist off the floor with elbows tracking about 45°. Press the floor away and lock out without the hips sagging.
trainerTip: Squeeze your glutes and brace — a push-up is a moving plank.

name: Push-Up Plus
setupNotes: Set a standard push-up position with hands directly under the shoulders. Brace hard before the first rep — there is no external load to do it for you.
targetNotes: Complete a full push-up, then at the top push the floor away extra so your shoulder blades spread wide. Let them retract before the next rep.
trainerTip: The plus is the point — it trains the serratus that keeps your scapula healthy under a bench press.

name: Rack Pull
setupNotes: Set the pins just below knee height and build your grip before the pull. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Break the bar off the pins and drive to lockout. Return it to dead rest on the pins every rep.
trainerTip: Load it heavy — this is top-end hip and back strength with the hardest centimetres cut out.

name: Rear Delt Fly
setupNotes: Hinge to 45° or rest chest-down on an incline bench with the weights hanging. Set the dumbbells within reach and plant your stance before you pick them up.
targetNotes: Raise the arms out to the sides with a soft elbow bend, squeezing the shoulder blades. Lower slowly.
trainerTip: Lead with the pinkies and think 'thumbs up' — it is a fly, not a row.

name: Recumbent Bike
setupNotes: Set the saddle so your knee keeps a slight bend at the bottom of the stroke. Set the saddle height so your knee keeps a slight bend at the bottom of the stroke.
targetNotes: Ride the planned interval or steady block. Track time and distance where the console allows.
trainerTip: The air bike punishes power output — great for intervals, brutal for the ego.

name: Renegade Row
setupNotes: Set a plank position with a dumbbell in each hand, feet wide for stability. Set the dumbbells within reach and plant your stance before you pick them up.
targetNotes: Row one bell to your hip while the body stays square to the floor. Lower and switch sides.
trainerTip: Anti-rotation under load — widen the feet before you widen the weights.

name: Reverse Crunch
setupNotes: Lie on your back with hips bent 90° and hands flat beside you. Brace hard before the first rep — there is no external load to do it for you.
targetNotes: Curl the knees toward the chest, lifting the hips off the floor. Lower without swinging.
trainerTip: The hips lifting is the rep — swinging the legs is just cardio.

name: Reverse Curl
setupNotes: Hold the weight with an overhand grip at arm's length. Choose the grip groove that keeps your wrists neutral.
targetNotes: Curl to shoulder height keeping the wrists straight and firm. Lower with control.
trainerTip: The forearms will give out first — that is the design, not a fault.

name: Reverse Hyperextension
setupNotes: Set your hips on the pad with the legs hanging below. Adjust the seat and handle height so the pad meets the working joint.
targetNotes: Swing the legs up to body height squeezing the glutes. Lower slowly under control.
trainerTip: Decompresses the spine while loading the glutes — a favourite after heavy deadlifts.

name: Reverse Lunge
setupNotes: Stand tall with the weight at your sides. Set the dumbbells within reach and plant your stance before you pick them up.
targetNotes: Step back and drop the rear knee to just above the floor. Drive back to standing off the front leg.
trainerTip: Reverse lunges are knee-friendlier than forward ones — same legs, less strain.

name: Reverse Pec Deck
setupNotes: Hinge to 45° or rest chest-down on an incline bench with the weights hanging. Adjust the seat and handle height so the pad meets the working joint.
targetNotes: Raise the arms out to the sides with a soft elbow bend, squeezing the shoulder blades. Lower slowly.
trainerTip: Lead with the pinkies and think 'thumbs up' — it is a fly, not a row.

name: Reverse-Grip Bench Press
setupNotes: Take an underhand grip slightly wider than shoulder width on the bar. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Lower the bar toward your lower chest with elbows tucked. Press up keeping the wrists strong and neutral.
trainerTip: Have a spotter the first time — the bar drifts toward your face if the wrists collapse.

name: Reverse-Grip Lat Pulldown
setupNotes: Take a supinated shoulder-width grip on the bar. Set the pulley height first, then test the travel with a light pin before loading.
targetNotes: Pull the bar to your upper chest squeezing the lats hard at the bottom. Return to a full stretch with control.
trainerTip: The underhand grip biases biceps and lower lats — a fine fill-in between chin-up sessions.

name: Romanian Deadlift
setupNotes: Stand tall holding the weight with knees softly unlocked. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Push the hips back, lowering the weight down your thighs until the hamstrings max out. Stand by driving the hips forward, not lifting with the back.
trainerTip: It is a hamstring stretch with load — the moment your back rounds, the rep is over.

name: Rope Pushdown
setupNotes: Face a high pulley with the straight bar attached and elbows pinned to your sides. Attach the rope and grip the ends neutrally, palms facing each other.
targetNotes: Extend to straight arms keeping the upper arms still. Let the weight return to a controlled 90°.
trainerTip: Pin the elbows — if they drift forward, the chest and lats start freelancing.

name: Rowing Machine
setupNotes: Set the damper, strap the feet in, and take the handle with a flat-back hinge. Set the damper and strap your feet in before the first stroke.
targetNotes: Drive legs, then back, then arms — and reverse the order on the recovery. Every stroke the same length.
trainerTip: The order never changes: legs, back, arms, arms, back, legs.

name: Running
setupNotes: Start with two minutes of easy jogging before touching any pace work. Brace hard before the first rep — there is no external load to do it for you.
targetNotes: Run at a conversational pace for base miles, or structured intervals for quality. Log distance and time.
trainerTip: Eighty percent easy running makes the fast twenty possible — most runners get this backwards.

name: Russian Twist
setupNotes: Sit with the knees bent, heels light on the floor, torso leaned back 45°. Choose a ball weight you can move fast or hold with control.
targetNotes: Rotate the weight side to side, touching the floor beside each hip. Move from the ribs.
trainerTip: A deliberate twist beats a blurry spin — slow it down until the obliques burn.

name: Scissor Kick
setupNotes: Lie on your back with hands under the hips and both legs lifted. Brace hard before the first rep — there is no external load to do it for you.
targetNotes: Sweep the legs past each other, one high one low, alternating the crossing point.
trainerTip: Keep the lower back welded to the floor — range follows control here.

name: Seal Row
setupNotes: Lie chest-down on a high bench with the bar hanging at arm's length beneath you. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Row the bar toward the underside of the bench until the plates near your chest. Lower fully without the torso helping.
trainerTip: Zero body English possible — pure back strength and an honest gauge of your row.

name: Seated Cable Row
setupNotes: Plant your feet on the platform and sit tall with a slight forward lean at the hips. Set the pulley height first, then test the travel with a light pin before loading.
targetNotes: Pull the handle to your navel driving the elbows past your ribs. Let the arms extend fully into a controlled stretch forward.
trainerTip: Chest out at the finish and spine long at the stretch — never round to gain distance.

name: Seated Calf Raise
setupNotes: Sit with the pad on your knees and the balls of your feet on the platform. Adjust the seat and handle height so the pad meets the working joint.
targetNotes: Lower the heels to a full stretch. Drive up onto the toes squeezing the soleus.
trainerTip: Seated targets the soleus — the endurance calf — so high reps rule here.

name: Seated Dumbbell Calf Raise
setupNotes: Sit with the pad on your knees and the balls of your feet on the platform. Set the dumbbells within reach and plant your stance before you pick them up.
targetNotes: Lower the heels to a full stretch. Drive up onto the toes squeezing the soleus.
trainerTip: Seated targets the soleus — the endurance calf — so high reps rule here.

name: Seated Dumbbell Curl
setupNotes: Sit tall on a bench with the dumbbells hanging at your sides. Set the dumbbells within reach and plant your stance before you pick them up.
targetNotes: Curl both up without torso swing. Lower to a full hang.
trainerTip: Sitting deletes the hip-hinge cheat — what is left is biceps.

name: Seated Dumbbell Shoulder Press
setupNotes: Sit tall on an upright bench with the dumbbells at shoulder height. Set the dumbbells within reach and plant your stance before you pick them up.
targetNotes: Press up and slightly together to lockout without clanking the bells. Lower to ear level.
trainerTip: Stop an inch shy of touching at the top — constant tension beats the sound effect.

name: Seated Lateral Raise
setupNotes: Sit tall on the end of a bench with the dumbbells hanging at your sides. Set the dumbbells within reach and plant your stance before you pick them up.
targetNotes: Raise the arms out to shoulder height with soft elbows. Lower slowly without swinging.
trainerTip: Sitting kills the hip swing — strict reps at strict heights.

name: Seated Leg Curl
setupNotes: Set the seat so the pad sits just above your heels with legs straight. Adjust the seat and handle height so the pad meets the working joint.
targetNotes: Curl down and under the seat to full contraction. Return to straight legs with control.
trainerTip: The seated angle stretches the hams at the hip — arguably the better curl.

name: Seated Overhead Press
setupNotes: Set the bench upright and rack the bar at chin height. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Press to lockout keeping your back in contact with the pad. Lower under control to the clavicles.
trainerTip: No leg drive means honest pressing — expect humbler numbers than standing.

name: Shadow Boxing
setupNotes: Set your stance and guard with light fists. Brace hard before the first rep — there is no external load to do it for you.
targetNotes: Throw combinations of jabs, crosses, and hooks while circling an imaginary opponent. Work in rounds.
trainerTip: Breathe out on every punch — the shoulders burn first, so pace the rounds.

name: Shrimp Squat
setupNotes: Stand on one leg holding the free foot behind you. Brace hard before the first rep — there is no external load to do it for you.
targetNotes: Squat down on the standing leg keeping the free foot close to your glute. Stand back up under control.
trainerTip: The pistol's awkward cousin — hold a support while you earn the balance.

name: Side Lunge
setupNotes: Stand tall with the weight held at your chest. Set the dumbbells within reach and plant your stance before you pick them up.
targetNotes: Step sideways, sitting into the lunging hip while the other leg stays straight. Push back to centre.
trainerTip: Sit back into the hip like a one-legged squat — do not just bend the knee sideways.

name: Side Plank
setupNotes: Stack the feet and rest on one forearm with the elbow under the shoulder. Brace hard before the first rep — there is no external load to do it for you.
targetNotes: Lift the hips until the head, hips and heels align. Hold for time.
trainerTip: Top hand on the hip or reaching skyward — both fine, sagging is not.

name: Side Plank Dip
setupNotes: Set a side plank on your forearm with feet stacked and hips high. Brace hard before the first rep — there is no external load to do it for you.
targetNotes: Drop the hips toward the floor, then drive them back up past neutral. Repeat with control.
trainerTip: Own the bottom of the dip — the obliques do their best work in the last inch.

name: Side-Lying Hip Abduction
setupNotes: Lie on your side with the body straight and the bottom arm supporting your head. Brace hard before the first rep — there is no external load to do it for you.
targetNotes: Lift the top leg to about 45° keeping the knee and toes pointing forward. Lower with control.
trainerTip: Small, honest range — rolling the hip back to lift higher is borrowing, not training.

name: Single-Arm Cable Row
setupNotes: Set a single handle at knee height and square your hips to the stack. Set the pulley height first, then test the travel with a light pin before loading.
targetNotes: Row the handle to your hip keeping the elbow close. Return to a full stretch without letting the torso rotate.
trainerTip: Fight the twist with your obliques — the anti-rotation is half the exercise.

name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Bench Press
setupNotes: Lie back on a flat bench holding one dumbbell at chest height, free hand braced. Set the dumbbells within reach and plant your stance before you pick them up.
targetNotes: Press the bell to lockout without letting the torso rotate. Lower under control.
trainerTip: The obliques fight the imbalance — a chest press with a core side-job.

name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Overhead Extension
setupNotes: Hold the weight overhead with both hands, elbows narrow and pointing forward. Set the dumbbells within reach and plant your stance before you pick them up.
targetNotes: Lower the weight behind your head by bending the elbows only. Extend to full lockout overhead.
trainerTip: The overhead position stretches the long head — the two-thirds of the triceps most lifts miss.

name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Shoulder Press
setupNotes: Hold one dumbbell at shoulder height with a braced, square stance. Set the dumbbells within reach and plant your stance before you pick them up.
targetNotes: Press overhead to lockout without leaning away. Lower under control to the start.
trainerTip: The obliques fight the tilt the whole time — one side at a time exposes the weak link.

name: Single-Arm Kettlebell Swing
setupNotes: Set the bell one shoe-length in front of you, hinge, and grip with both hands. Grip high on the handle and keep your wrist straight throughout.
targetNotes: Hike the bell back between your legs, then snap the hips forward to swing it to chest height. Let it fall and re-hinge.
trainerTip: It is a hinge, not a squat, and a hip snap, not an arm lift — the bell floats up on momentum.

name: Single-Arm Landmine Press
setupNotes: Load one end of a bar in a landmine and hold the sleeve at shoulder height. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Press up and forward along the bar's natural arc to extension. Lower with control.
trainerTip: The angled path spares cranky shoulders while pressing hard — a rehab-room hero.

name: Single-Arm Lat Pulldown
setupNotes: Centre a single handle and grip it with the working side's hand. Set the pulley height first, then test the travel with a light pin before loading.
targetNotes: Pull the handle down to your shoulder driving the elbow into your pocket. Let it rise to a full lat stretch.
trainerTip: Feel the lat stretch on every rep — range beats weight here.

name: Single-Arm Machine Row
setupNotes: Set the seat so the handle sits at hip height and brace with your free hand. Adjust the seat and handle height so the pad meets the working joint.
targetNotes: Row the handle to your hip through the longest range the machine allows. Return slowly to a full stretch.
trainerTip: One side at a time exposes side-to-side gaps — match your reps to the weaker arm.

name: Single-Arm Pushdown
setupNotes: Face a high pulley with the straight bar attached and elbows pinned to your sides. Set the pulley height first, then test the travel with a light pin before loading.
targetNotes: Extend to straight arms keeping the upper arms still. Let the weight return to a controlled 90°.
trainerTip: Pin the elbows — if they drift forward, the chest and lats start freelancing.

name: Single-Leg Calf Raise
setupNotes: Set the pads over your shoulders (or hold the weight) with the balls of your feet on the edge. Brace hard before the first rep — there is no external load to do it for you.
targetNotes: Drop the heels to a full stretch. Press up onto the toes as high as possible.
trainerTip: Pause one full second at the top and the bottom — bouncing is the calf-raise cheat code.

name: Single-Leg Extension
setupNotes: Set the pad just above your ankles and adjust the seat back. Adjust the seat and handle height so the pad meets the working joint.
targetNotes: Extend to a full lockout and squeeze the quad for a beat. Lower under control, never dropping the stack.
trainerTip: Pause at the top — riding the machine's momentum is why legs do not grow.

name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
setupNotes: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat and close to your hips. Brace hard before the first rep — there is no external load to do it for you.
targetNotes: Drive through the heels lifting the hips to a straight line. Squeeze the glutes at the top, then lower slowly.
trainerTip: Squeeze at the top like you are pinching a coin — two seconds minimum.

name: Single-Leg Hip Thrust
setupNotes: Set your upper back on a bench with one foot planted and the other leg held high. Check the bench angle and anchor points before you set up.
targetNotes: Drive through the planted foot to full hip lockout. Lower to a hover and repeat.
trainerTip: The raised leg steals stability — slow reps expose and fix it.

name: Single-Leg Press
setupNotes: Set your back flat on the seat with feet shoulder-width on the platform. Adjust the seat and handle height so the pad meets the working joint.
targetNotes: Lower the sled until the knees reach your chest without the hips rolling up. Press to just short of locked knees.
trainerTip: Butt lifting off the seat at the bottom means the range is too big for today — back the depth off.

name: Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift
setupNotes: Hold the weight on one side and stand on the opposite leg. Set the dumbbells within reach and plant your stance before you pick them up.
targetNotes: Hinge forward on one leg with the free leg extending behind you. Feel the working hamstring load, then stand tall.
trainerTip: Slow beats heavy — a wobbly single-leg RDL trains nothing but excuses.

name: Sissy Squat
setupNotes: Hold a support at chest height with feet hip-width and heels together. Brace hard before the first rep — there is no external load to do it for you.
targetNotes: Rise onto the balls of your feet and lean back into deep knee flexion. Pull back up with the quads.
trainerTip: The most direct quad stretch-and-load there is — depth comes slowly.

name: Sit-Up
setupNotes: Bend the knees, anchor the feet lightly, and set the hands by the ears. Brace hard before the first rep — there is no external load to do it for you.
targetNotes: Sit all the way up to a tall torso. Lower under control until the shoulder blades touch.
trainerTip: If your feet fly up, cross the arms over the chest or brace them under a bench.

name: Skater Hops
setupNotes: Stand on one leg with a slight knee bend and arms ready. Brace hard before the first rep — there is no external load to do it for you.
targetNotes: Bound laterally onto the other foot, absorbing the landing softly. Bound back the other way.
trainerTip: Stick each landing for a beat — lateral power is trained, not spilled.

name: Ski Erg
setupNotes: Set the damper and grip the handles at hip height. Adjust the seat and handle height so the pad meets the working joint.
targetNotes: Drive down with the whole body — legs, hips and arms finishing together. Track distance and time.
trainerTip: The same discipline as rowing — power through the middle, easy at the ends.

name: Skull Crusher
setupNotes: Lie on a bench holding the weight above your chest with arms roughly perpendicular to the floor. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Lower the weight behind your forehead by bending only the elbows. Extend back to straight arms.
trainerTip: The elbows stay put and point at the ceiling — flaring them forward shifts stress to the joints.

name: Sled Pull
setupNotes: Attach the strap or handles to the sled and set your stance. Load the sled evenly and check your runway is clear.
targetNotes: Pull hand over hand, or walk the sled toward you with strong steps, keeping constant tension.
trainerTip: Face backward to hammer the quads, forward to drag the posterior chain into it.

name: Sled Push
setupNotes: Load the sled evenly and set your hands low on the uprights with a strong forward lean. Load the sled evenly and check your runway is clear.
targetNotes: Drive the sled with short, powerful steps and the body around 45°. Push for distance or time.
trainerTip: Keep the arms straight and push through the ground — it is a moving leg press.

name: Slider Leg Curl
setupNotes: Lie on your back with a slider or towel under each heel and hips lifted to a line. Set the gear up within reach so the set starts without scrambling.
targetNotes: Slide the heels out to straight legs, then curl them back under the hips without letting the hips drop.
trainerTip: Floor-based and joint-friendly — the hips staying tall is the rep counter's honesty check.

name: Smith Machine Bench Press
setupNotes: Lie back with your eyes just under the bar and drive your shoulder blades down and together. Set the safety stops just short of your end range before adding load.
targetNotes: Lower the weight to mid-chest with elbows about 45° from your torso. Press up and slightly back to lockout without losing the packed shoulders.
trainerTip: Grip wide enough that your forearms stay vertical at the bottom, and only use depth you can control every single rep.

name: Smith Machine Calf Raise
setupNotes: Set the pads over your shoulders (or hold the weight) with the balls of your feet on the edge. Set the safety stops just short of your end range before adding load.
targetNotes: Drop the heels to a full stretch. Press up onto the toes as high as possible.
trainerTip: Pause one full second at the top and the bottom — bouncing is the calf-raise cheat code.

name: Smith Machine Close-Grip Press
setupNotes: Grip the bar just inside shoulder width and set your usual bench position. Set the safety stops just short of your end range before adding load.
targetNotes: Lower to your lower chest with the elbows tucked. Press up keeping the wrists stacked over the elbows.
trainerTip: Shoulder-width, not hands-touching — 'close' is relative to your bench.

name: Smith Machine Decline Press
setupNotes: Lock your ankles under the pads and keep your hips planted on the decline bench. Set the safety stops just short of your end range before adding load.
targetNotes: Lower the weight to your lower chest on a controlled path. Press up through the same groove, thinking about the lower pec line.
trainerTip: The range is shorter than flat bench — recalibrate your warm-up weights before loading heavy.

name: Smith Machine Incline Bench Press
setupNotes: Set the bench to a 30–45° angle and plant your feet firmly on the floor. Set the safety stops just short of your end range before adding load.
targetNotes: Lower the weight to your upper chest, keeping elbows under the wrists. Press up in a slight arc toward eye level.
trainerTip: Stop the set when your shoulders creep up toward your ears — that is the incline stealing your press.

name: Smith Machine Overhead Press
setupNotes: Rack the bar on your front delts with elbows slightly ahead of it and feet hip-width. Set the safety stops just short of your end range before adding load.
targetNotes: Press the bar overhead, moving your head back as it passes, finishing with biceps by the ears. Lock out tall with the ribs down.
trainerTip: Squeeze the glutes and brace — a leaking midsection steals more press than weak shoulders do.

name: Smith Machine Romanian Deadlift
setupNotes: Stand tall holding the weight with knees softly unlocked. Set the safety stops just short of your end range before adding load.
targetNotes: Push the hips back, lowering the weight down your thighs until the hamstrings max out. Stand by driving the hips forward, not lifting with the back.
trainerTip: It is a hamstring stretch with load — the moment your back rounds, the rep is over.

name: Smith Machine Row
setupNotes: Hinge to roughly 45° or flatter and brace your trunk before you touch the weight. Set the safety stops just short of your end range before adding load.
targetNotes: Drive your elbows back past your torso until the weight reaches your lower ribs. Lower under control to a full stretch without rounding.
trainerTip: Row with a still torso — if your hips pump, the load is writing cheques your back cannot cash.

name: Smith Machine Shrug
setupNotes: Stand tall holding the weight with your shoulders pulled down and back. Set the safety stops just short of your end range before adding load.
targetNotes: Shrug your shoulders straight up toward your ears. Lower to a full stretch with control.
trainerTip: Straight up and straight down — rolling the shoulders adds injury risk, not growth.

name: Smith Machine Squat
setupNotes: Set the bar across your traps, unrack, and take a stance just outside shoulder width. Set the safety stops just short of your end range before adding load.
targetNotes: Sit down between your hips until the hip crease passes the knee, or as deep as your back stays neutral. Drive up through mid-foot to stand tall.
trainerTip: Own the depth where you can keep a neutral spine — deeper at lighter load beats higher at max.

name: Smith Machine Upright Row
setupNotes: Stand square to the smith bar with an overhand shoulder-width grip. Set the safety stops just short of your end range before adding load.
targetNotes: Pull the bar straight up to chest height keeping the elbows above the hands. Lower with control.
trainerTip: The fixed path removes the wobble — stop at chest height and keep the wrists loose.

name: Snatch-Grip Deadlift
setupNotes: Grip the bar snatch-wide and pull the slack out with a tall chest. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Deadlift with the wide grip keeping the bar close and the back flat. Finish standing tall.
trainerTip: A brutal upper-back builder — start conservative, because the wide grip punishes position.

name: Spider Curl
setupNotes: Set an incline bench steep and lie chest-down with the arms hanging straight. Set the dumbbells within reach and plant your stance before you pick them up.
targetNotes: Curl to shoulder height with zero elbow swing. Lower to a dead hang.
trainerTip: The strictest curl in the building — pick weights accordingly.

name: Split Squat
setupNotes: Step one foot forward into a long stance with the rear heel up. Set the dumbbells within reach and plant your stance before you pick them up.
targetNotes: Lower straight down until the rear knee nearly touches the floor. Press back up through both legs with the front leg dominant.
trainerTip: Front shin stays roughly vertical — if the knee runs far forward, take a longer step.

name: Sprint Intervals
setupNotes: Warm up thoroughly — strides and drills before any all-out effort. Brace hard before the first rep — there is no external load to do it for you.
targetNotes: Alternate maximal sprints with walk-back recovery. Track distance and total time.
trainerTip: Full recovery between reps keeps every sprint fast — this is power work, not cardio.

name: Stability Ball Crunch
setupNotes: Sit on the ball and walk the feet out until the lower back rests on the curve. Set the gear up within reach so the set starts without scrambling.
targetNotes: Crunch the ribs toward the hips over the ball. Lower into the stretch.
trainerTip: The ball's curve stretches what the floor cannot — use that stretch.

name: Stability Ball Leg Curl
setupNotes: Lie on your back with heels on the ball and hips lifted into a straight line. Set the gear up within reach so the set starts without scrambling.
targetNotes: Curl the ball toward your hips keeping the hips high. Roll it back out to straight legs.
trainerTip: The hips never drop — this one is a hamstring curl and a glute bridge at once.

name: Stability Ball Pike
setupNotes: Walk out into a plank with the shins on the ball and hands under the shoulders. Set the gear up within reach so the set starts without scrambling.
targetNotes: Drive the hips up into a pike, rolling the ball toward the hands. Roll back to the long plank.
trainerTip: Hips high and back flat on the way up — bend at the hips, never the spine.

name: Stability Ball Plank
setupNotes: Set the forearms on the ball and step the feet back into a long line. Set the gear up within reach so the set starts without scrambling.
targetNotes: Hold the plank with the ball still — any wobble travels straight to the core.
trainerTip: Shorter holds and stiller ball beat long, shaky ones.

name: Stability Ball Rollout
setupNotes: Kneel with the forearms on the ball and the body leaning into it. Set the gear up within reach so the set starts without scrambling.
targetNotes: Roll forward letting the ball travel along the forearms, ribs down. Pull back with the abs before the back arches.
trainerTip: The wheel's gentler cousin — same law applies: the spine never arches.

name: Stair Climber
setupNotes: Step on and set the pace before releasing the rails. Adjust the seat and handle height so the pad meets the working joint.
targetNotes: Climb at a steady rate with a tall posture, hands off the rails. Track time.
trainerTip: Leaning on the rails halves the work — light fingertips at most.

name: Stair Runs
setupNotes: Find a safe flight of stairs or stadium steps with a clear landing. Brace hard before the first rep — there is no external load to do it for you.
targetNotes: Sprint up the flight with powerful strides, then walk down to recover. Repeat for the planned reps.
trainerTip: Walk the descents — the down is the rest, the up is the work.

name: Standing Calf Raise
setupNotes: Set the pads over your shoulders (or hold the weight) with the balls of your feet on the edge. Adjust the seat and handle height so the pad meets the working joint.
targetNotes: Drop the heels to a full stretch. Press up onto the toes as high as possible.
trainerTip: Pause one full second at the top and the bottom — bouncing is the calf-raise cheat code.

name: Standing Leg Curl
setupNotes: Set the ankle cuff on the low pulley and stand facing the stack. Set the pulley height first, then test the travel with a light pin before loading.
targetNotes: Curl the cuffed heel toward your glute keeping the thighs still. Return to a long leg with control.
trainerTip: One leg at a time spots side-to-side gaps — train the weaker one first.

name: Stationary Bike
setupNotes: Set the saddle so your knee keeps a slight bend at the bottom of the stroke. Set the saddle height so your knee keeps a slight bend at the bottom of the stroke.
targetNotes: Ride the planned interval or steady block. Track time and distance where the console allows.
trainerTip: The air bike punishes power output — great for intervals, brutal for the ego.

name: Step-Up
setupNotes: Set a box at knee height and place your whole foot on top. Set the box on a flat, non-slip surface before you start.
targetNotes: Drive through the top leg to stand fully tall over the box. Lower with the same leg — no push-off from the floor.
trainerTip: No bouncing off the bottom leg — that is a cheating hand on the scales.

name: Stiff-Leg Deadlift
setupNotes: Set up as a deadlift, then stand with the knees nearly locked. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Hinge the bar down your shins to mid-shin or your lower-back tolerance. Pull to standing keeping the spine flat.
trainerTip: Stiffer knees shift the load lower into the hamstrings — respect the smaller margin for form.

name: Straight-Arm Pulldown
setupNotes: Stand facing a high pulley with a bar or rope, arms straight, hinged slightly forward. Set the pulley height first, then test the travel with a light pin before loading.
targetNotes: Sweep the handle down to your thighs without bending the elbows. Let it rise to shoulder height for a full lat stretch.
trainerTip: If you cannot keep straight arms, the stack is too heavy — ego down, lats up.

name: Suitcase Carry
setupNotes: Deadlift one weight to your side and brace the opposite obliques. Set the dumbbells within reach and plant your stance before you pick them up.
targetNotes: Walk staying perfectly level — no leaning away from or into the load. Put it down square, never a drop.
trainerTip: The free side working overtime is the point — a moving side plank.

name: Sumo Deadlift
setupNotes: Take a wide stance with toes out and grip inside your legs. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Push the knees out and wedge the hips down as the bar leaves the floor. Lock out tall without dumping the chest.
trainerTip: Hip structure decides sumo vs conventional — pick the groove where you are strongest, not what looks cooler.

name: Sumo Squat
setupNotes: Take a wide stance with toes turned out and the weight held at your chest. Set the dumbbells within reach and plant your stance before you pick them up.
targetNotes: Sit straight down between your hips to your full range. Drive up pressing the knees out.
trainerTip: Knees track over the little toes — if they cave in, narrow the stance.

name: Superman
setupNotes: Lie face-down with the arms extended overhead and legs straight. Brace hard before the first rep — there is no external load to do it for you.
targetNotes: Lift the arms, chest and legs off the floor into a gentle arc. Hold for time, then lower.
trainerTip: Reach long rather than high — the goal is extension, not altitude.

name: Suspension Trainer Chest Fly
setupNotes: Set the straps mid-length and lean in with arms spread wide, palms facing in. Set the gear up within reach so the set starts without scrambling.
targetNotes: Sweep the handles down and together in a wide arc until they meet below your chest. Open back to the stretch.
trainerTip: Keep the arc wide and the body one plank — the straps punish a sagging midsection.

name: Suspension Trainer Curl
setupNotes: Set the straps mid-length and lean back holding the handles with palms up. Set the gear up within reach so the set starts without scrambling.
targetNotes: Curl your body upright keeping the body rigid and the elbows high. Lower with control.
trainerTip: Your bodyweight is the load — walk the feet forward to add plates, so to speak.

name: Suspension Trainer Hamstring Curl
setupNotes: Lie on your back with the heels in the straps and hips lifted to a straight line. Set the gear up within reach so the set starts without scrambling.
targetNotes: Curl the heels toward your hips keeping the hips tall. Extend back out without sagging.
trainerTip: The straps make the curl unstable — the hips staying high is the whole exercise.

name: Suspension Trainer Push-Up
setupNotes: Set the straps mid-length and lean into the handles directly under your shoulders. Set the gear up within reach so the set starts without scrambling.
targetNotes: Lower your chest between the handles keeping the body rigid. Press back to straight arms.
trainerTip: The instability recruits every pressing helper you own — walk the feet in to load it up.

name: Suspension Trainer Row
setupNotes: Set the straps to mid length and lean back holding the handles with arms straight. Set the gear up within reach so the set starts without scrambling.
targetNotes: Pull your chest up between the handles with elbows tucked at 45°. Lower with control keeping the body straight.
trainerTip: The more horizontal your body, the harder it gets — angle is your weight stack.

name: Suspension Trainer Triceps Extension
setupNotes: Set the straps mid-length, lean in holding the handles, and lock the body straight. Set the gear up within reach so the set starts without scrambling.
targetNotes: Bend only the elbows, lowering your forehead between the handles. Extend back to straight arms.
trainerTip: The lean angle is the load — walk the feet back when the set gets easy.

name: Svend Press
setupNotes: Stand tall holding a plate between your palms at chest height. Pick a plate you can hold securely for the whole set.
targetNotes: Press the plate out to arm's length while squeezing inward. Bring it back to your chest under control.
trainerTip: Use a light plate and slow reps — this is a finisher, not a strength builder.

name: Swimming
setupNotes: Goggles on — pick your stroke and mind the lane etiquette. Brace hard before the first rep — there is no external load to do it for you.
targetNotes: Swim the planned distance with even strokes. Track distance and total time.
trainerTip: Count strokes per lap — fewer strokes at the same speed means better technique.

name: T-Bar Row
setupNotes: Straddle the bar or T-bar station and hinge to about 45° with a neutral spine. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Row the weight to your sternum keeping the elbows close. Lower to full arm extension without your chest dropping.
trainerTip: A full stack of small plates beats two monsters on the sleeve — depth of stretch is the goal.

name: Thruster
setupNotes: Front-rack the bar with elbows high and a squat-width stance. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Squat to full depth and drive the bar overhead in one continuous motion. Lower to the rack and repeat.
trainerTip: One rep, two lifts — the squat throws, the shoulders catch. Breathe on a rhythm.

name: Toes to Bar
setupNotes: Hang from the bar with an overhand, slightly wide grip. Wipe the bar and set your grip width before you jump up.
targetNotes: Raise straight legs all the way to touch the bar. Lower slowly to a dead hang.
trainerTip: If touching is a bridge too far, toes-to-horizontal is honest progress.

name: Trap Bar Curl
setupNotes: Stand tall with the weight at arm's length and the elbows pinned to your ribs. Centre yourself between the handles and set a tripod foot before you brace.
targetNotes: Curl to shoulder height without letting the elbows travel forward. Lower all the way to straight arms.
trainerTip: The elbows are hinges bolted to your sides — every inch they drift forward steals biceps.

name: Trap Bar Deadlift
setupNotes: Stand with the bar over mid-foot, shins a hand-width from the steel, and hinge down to grip. Centre yourself between the handles and set a tripod foot before you brace.
targetNotes: Push the floor away keeping the bar dragging up your legs. Lock out tall with the glutes, not a lean-back.
trainerTip: The bar never leaves your legs — treat every millimetre of daylight as a technique fault.

name: Trap Bar Farmer's Walk
setupNotes: Deadlift the weights to your sides and stand tall before the first step. Centre yourself between the handles and set a tripod foot before you brace.
targetNotes: Walk with short, quick steps keeping the shoulders back and spine tall. Set the weights down only when the set ends.
trainerTip: Grip gives out before legs usually — chalk on, straps off, unless it is a dedicated grip day.

name: Trap Bar Shrug
setupNotes: Stand tall holding the weight with your shoulders pulled down and back. Centre yourself between the handles and set a tripod foot before you brace.
targetNotes: Shrug your shoulders straight up toward your ears. Lower to a full stretch with control.
trainerTip: Straight up and straight down — rolling the shoulders adds injury risk, not growth.

name: Treadmill Run
setupNotes: Set your pace and incline before stepping onto the belt. Clip the safety key and set the belt speed before you step on.
targetNotes: Hold the programmed pace with the same form you would use on the road. Note distance and time.
trainerTip: One percent incline roughly offsets the belt's assist — closer to outdoor effort.

name: Treadmill Walk
setupNotes: Set the belt speed and incline before you step on. Clip the safety key and set the belt speed before you step on.
targetNotes: Walk at your target pace with a tall posture, hands off the rails. Track distance and time.
trainerTip: Crank the incline before the speed — a steep walk rivals a slow jog for effort.

name: Triceps Dip
setupNotes: Support yourself on parallel bars with the torso upright and shoulders down. Test the bar height and lock your shoulders down before descending.
targetNotes: Lower until the elbows reach about 90°. Press to lockout without shrugging.
trainerTip: An upright torso keeps it triceps; leaning forward recruits the chest.

name: Triceps Kickback
setupNotes: Hinge over with the elbows bent and pinned at your sides. Set the dumbbells within reach and plant your stance before you pick them up.
targetNotes: Extend both arms straight back, squeezing the triceps at the top. Return only to the elbow bend.
trainerTip: The upper arm stays frozen like a statue — everything else is decoration.

name: Tuck Jump
setupNotes: Set your feet hip-width with knees soft and arms ready. Brace hard before the first rep — there is no external load to do it for you.
targetNotes: Jump vertically pulling the knees to chest height. Land softly into the next rep.
trainerTip: Land quiet and land low — a loud tuck jump is a crash you repeated.

name: Turkish Get-Up
setupNotes: Lie down with the bell pressed overhead in one hand and the same-side knee bent. Grip high on the handle and keep your wrist straight throughout.
targetNotes: Roll to the elbow, then the hand, bridge up to kneeling, and stand — never letting your eyes leave the bell. Reverse every step back to the floor.
trainerTip: Slow is the whole exercise — five clean reps per side beats ten rushed ones.

name: Underhand Barbell Row
setupNotes: Hinge to about 45° and take an underhand grip just outside shoulder width. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Pull the bar to your lower abdomen driving the elbows back. Lower slowly with the torso angle fixed.
trainerTip: The supinated grip lets you use more load — earn it with a rigid torso, not a heave.

name: Upright Row
setupNotes: Hold the weight in front of your thighs with an overhand grip. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Pull straight up to chest height keeping the elbows above the hands. Lower slowly.
trainerTip: Stop at chest height — pulling to the chin is where shoulders start complaining.

name: V-Bar Lat Pulldown
setupNotes: Clip the V-bar on and sit with your thighs locked in. Set the pulley height first, then test the travel with a light pin before loading.
targetNotes: Pull the V-bar to your sternum with elbows driving down. Return to a full stretch without letting the shoulders shrug.
trainerTip: Elbows to the pockets — the V-bar keeps you honest on the path.

name: V-Bar Pushdown
setupNotes: Face a high pulley with the straight bar attached and elbows pinned to your sides. Set the pulley height first, then test the travel with a light pin before loading.
targetNotes: Extend to straight arms keeping the upper arms still. Let the weight return to a controlled 90°.
trainerTip: Pin the elbows — if they drift forward, the chest and lats start freelancing.

name: V-Up
setupNotes: Lie flat with the arms extended overhead and legs straight. Brace hard before the first rep — there is no external load to do it for you.
targetNotes: Fold in half, touching the toes with the fingers at the top. Lower both ends under control.
trainerTip: Lower slowly — the descent is half the exercise.

name: Waiter's Carry
setupNotes: Press a bell or dumbbell overhead with a locked, stacked arm. Grip high on the handle and keep your wrist straight throughout.
targetNotes: Walk with the weight overhead and the ribs stacked over the hips. Set it down only when the set ends.
trainerTip: The overhead march builds the stability your press has been missing.

name: Walking
setupNotes: Shoes on, tall posture, arms free to swing. Brace hard before the first rep — there is no external load to do it for you.
targetNotes: Walk at a brisk but sustainable pace. Track distance and time.
trainerTip: Daily walks are the cheapest fitness upgrade there is — zero recovery cost.

name: Walking Lunge
setupNotes: Stand tall with the weight held at your sides or in the front rack. Set the dumbbells within reach and plant your stance before you pick them up.
targetNotes: Step forward and lower until the back knee hovers at the floor. Push through the front leg to step into the next rep.
trainerTip: Long steps bias the glutes and short steps the quads — choose on purpose.

name: Wall Ball
setupNotes: Stand a pace from a solid wall holding the ball at your chest. Choose a ball weight you can move fast or hold with control.
targetNotes: Squat below parallel and drive the ball to a target overhead, catching it back into the squat. Repeat fluidly.
trainerTip: Catch and squat in one motion — the ball never rests in your hands.

name: Wall Push-Up
setupNotes: Stand an arm's length from a wall with palms on it at chest height. Brace hard before the first rep — there is no external load to do it for you.
targetNotes: Bend the elbows to bring the chest toward the wall keeping a rigid line from heels to head. Press back out.
trainerTip: The gentlest pressing regression there is — perfect for rehab or the very first sessions.

name: Wall Sit
setupNotes: Stand against a wall and slide down until your thighs are parallel. Brace hard before the first rep — there is no external load to do it for you.
targetNotes: Hold the thighs level with knees over the ankles for time. Keep your back flat against the wall.
trainerTip: The burn means it is working — shift the weight onto your heels if the knees complain.

name: Weighted Chin-Up
setupNotes: Add a plate via belt or hold a dumbbell between your thighs. Pick a plate you can hold securely for the whole set.
targetNotes: Chin over bar with the extra load locked tight. Lower to a full hang without letting the weight swing.
trainerTip: Log the added load in the weight field and compare against bodyweight sessions to see true gains.

name: Weighted Plank
setupNotes: Set a standard plank with a plate centred on your mid-back. Pick a plate you can hold securely for the whole set.
targetNotes: Hold the rigid line under load. Have a partner add or remove the plate between sets.
trainerTip: If the hips dip under the plate, the load outranks your brace — lighten it.

name: Weighted Pull-Up
setupNotes: Hang a plate from a belt or clamp a dumbbell between your thighs before you grip the bar. Pick a plate you can hold securely for the whole set.
targetNotes: Pull to chin over bar with the added load held tight. Lower to a full hang without swinging the weight.
trainerTip: Drop the belt when form slips — strict bodyweight reps first, iron second.

name: Weighted Push-Up
setupNotes: Set hands just outside shoulder width and step your feet back into one straight line. Have a partner centre the plate on your upper back, or load a weight vest, before you set your plank.
targetNotes: Lower until your chest is a fist off the floor with elbows tracking about 45°. Press the floor away and lock out without the hips sagging.
trainerTip: Squeeze your glutes and brace — a push-up is a moving plank.

name: Weighted Sit-Up
setupNotes: Hold a plate at your chest in sit-up position with the feet anchored. Pick a plate you can hold securely for the whole set.
targetNotes: Sit up to a tall torso keeping the plate pinned. Lower under control to the floor.
trainerTip: The plate at the chest is honest — arms overhead only when the basics are owned.

name: Wide Push-Up
setupNotes: Set your hands half a hand-width wider than your normal push-up position. Brace hard before the first rep — there is no external load to do it for you.
targetNotes: Lower the chest between the hands with a proud chest. Press up to full lockout keeping the body rigid.
trainerTip: The wider grip loads the chest more — a stepping stone toward full push-up strength.

name: Wide-Grip Barbell Row
setupNotes: Hinge to about 45° and take a grip well outside shoulder width. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Pull the bar to your sternum with high elbows. Lower under control to full arms.
trainerTip: The wide grip shifts the load up the back — pair it with narrower rows in the week.

name: Wide-Grip Bench Press
setupNotes: Grip the bar roughly a hand-width outside your normal bench width. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Lower to the chest with forearms vertical at the bottom. Press up in your usual arc with elbows flared by design.
trainerTip: Respect the shoulders — this variation punishes a sloppy warm-up.

name: Wide-Grip Curl
setupNotes: Take a grip well outside shoulder width on the bar. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Curl up with the elbows tracking slightly out. Lower fully to straight arms.
trainerTip: The wide grip shifts leverage onto the inner biceps head — subtle but real.

name: Wide-Grip Lat Pulldown
setupNotes: Grip the bar near the bends and lean back about ten degrees. Set the pulley height first, then test the travel with a light pin before loading.
targetNotes: Pull the bar to your upper chest with elbows driving out and down. Control the return to a full overhead stretch.
trainerTip: If your forearms burn before your lats, narrow the grip by a finger or two.

name: Wide-Grip Pull-Up
setupNotes: Hang with an overhand grip near the bar ends. Wipe the bar and set your grip width before you jump up.
targetNotes: Pull your chest toward the bar with elbows driving out. Lower under control to a full hang.
trainerTip: Tougher than the standard pull-up — treat it as a strength move, not a rep race.

name: Wide-Grip Seated Cable Row
setupNotes: Attach a long bar and grip outside shoulder width, seated tall. Set the pulley height first, then test the travel with a light pin before loading.
targetNotes: Pull the bar to your sternum with high elbows. Extend fully forward keeping the back flat.
trainerTip: Elbows high hits the upper back — pair it with lat-focused rows in the same week.

name: Windshield Wiper
setupNotes: Hang from a bar with a shoulder-width grip. Wipe the bar and set your grip width before you jump up.
targetNotes: Swing straight legs from side to side while keeping the shoulders level. Control both directions of the arc.
trainerTip: Start with bent knees and small arcs — this move has a black-belt requirement.

name: Wrist Roller
setupNotes: Hold the roller at shoulder height with a plate suspended on its cord. Set the gear up within reach so the set starts without scrambling.
targetNotes: Roll the cord up hand over hand until the plate touches the roller, then reverse it back down.
trainerTip: Burn now, crush later — grip day's least glamorous, most effective tool.

name: Zercher Squat
setupNotes: Cradle the bar in the crooks of your elbows with hands crossed and arms tight to the ribs. Load the bar symmetrically and set the hooks at a height you can unrack with straight arms.
targetNotes: Squat to depth keeping the chest tall over the cradled bar. Stand driving through the whole foot.
trainerTip: The bar in the elbows is uncomfortable by design — the squat pattern becomes brutally upright.

name: Zottman Curl
setupNotes: Hold the dumbbells at your sides with a supinated grip. Set the dumbbells within reach and plant your stance before you pick them up.
targetNotes: Curl up normally, then rotate the palms to face down at the top. Lower slowly in the pronated grip.
trainerTip: The slow reverse-grip descent builds the forearms while the curl builds biceps — two for one.
